They asked him for a sign, so he described Bayt al-Maqdis to them and mentioned to them the story of the caravan. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughira said: 'This is a sorcerer.' So Allah revealed to him: ﴿And We did not make the vision﴾," the verse.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Sahl ibn Sa'd, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw the Banu Fulan leaping upon his pulpit like monkeys, and that distressed him, and he was never seen laughing again until he died. So Allah revealed: ﴿And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people﴾."

Ibn Kathir, after citing its chain, said: "This chain is extremely weak. He mentioned among the men of the chain Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Zabban, who is abandoned (matruk), and his shaykh Abd al-Muhaymin ibn Abbas ibn Sahl ibn Sa'd, who is extremely weak."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Amr that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I saw the sons of al-Hakam ibn Abi al-As on the pulpits like monkeys, so Allah revealed: ﴿And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people and the cursed tree﴾," meaning al-Hakam and his offspring.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ya'la ibn Murra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I saw the Banu Umayya on the pulpits of the earth, and they will rule over you, and you will find them to be lords of evil." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was concerned about that, so Allah revealed the verse.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from al-Husayn ibn Ali something similar, raised (marfu'), but it is mursal (its chain lacks a Companion).

Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi and Ibn Asakir narrated from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib something similar, and it is mursal.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Aisha that she said to Marwan ibn al-Hakam: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say to your father and your grandfather: 'You are the cursed tree in the Qur'an.'" In this there is an oddity (nakara) in her words "he said to your father and your grandfather," and perhaps the grandfather of Marwan did not live to the time of prophethood.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, that he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was shown that he, and his companions, entered Makkah, while he was at that time in Madina. He set out for Makkah before the appointed time, and the polytheists turned him back. Some people said: 'He has been turned back, and he had told us that he would enter it.' So his return became a trial for them." These narrations conflict and it is not possible to reconcile them, so the obligation is to resort to preponderance (tarjih), and the more preponderant in number and soundness is that the occasion of revelation of this verse is the story of the Night Journey, so that is what is determined.

Ibn Kathir has related the consensus (ijma') of the authoritative scholars of interpretation on this regarding the vision, and regarding the interpretation of the tree, that it is the tree of al-Zaqqum, so no weight is given to anyone else alongside them.

Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Jahl said, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mentioned the tree of al-Zaqqum as a warning to them: "O assembly of Quraysh, do you know what the tree of al-Zaqqum is with which Muhammad frightens you?" They said: "No." He said: "Dates of Yathrib with butter. By Allah, if we gain control of it, we will devour it completely." Allah the Glorified said: ﴿Indeed, the tree of al-Zaqqum, the food of the sinful﴾ [al-Dukhan: 43–44]. And He revealed: ﴿And the cursed tree in the Qur'an﴾, the verse.

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him regarding His words ﴿And the cursed tree﴾, that he said: "Cursed, because He said: ﴿its shoots are like the heads of devils﴾ [al-Saffat: 65], and the devils are cursed."

**Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 17, verses 56–60 (part 1 of 2):**

.

His saying: ﴿Say: Call upon those you claim besides Him﴾. This is a refutation of a group of the polytheists who worshipped images that they believed to be representations of the angels, and of a group of the People of the Book who said that ʿIsa (Jesus), Maryam (Mary) and ʿUzayr (Ezra) were divine. Allah, glorified is He, commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to say to them: "Call upon those you claim are gods besides Allah." It was also said that by "those you claim" He meant a company of jinn whom some of the Arabs claimed to be with them. The verse is restricted to those mentioned earlier because of His saying: ﴿They seek the means of access to their Lord﴾, for this does not befit inanimate objects. ﴿Then they have no power to remove the harm from you﴾, meaning they are not able to do so. The true object of worship is the one who has the power to remove harm and to change one state into another and one place into another. It is therefore necessary to conclude with certainty that what you claim to be gods are not gods.

Then, glorified is He, emphasised their lack of power by showing the extent of their need for Allah in bringing benefits and warding off harms, so He said: ﴿Those whom they call upon, they seek the means of access to their Lord﴾. Here ﴿those﴾ (ulaʾika) is the subject (mubtadaʾ), and ﴿whom they call upon﴾ (alladhina yadʿuna) is its qualifying clause (ṣifa), with the relative pronoun (ḍamir al-ṣila) omitted, meaning "whom they call upon." The predicate of the subject is ﴿they seek the means of access to their Lord﴾ (yabtaghuna ila rabbihimu al-wasilah). It is also permissible for ﴿whom they call upon﴾ (alladhina yadʿuna) to be the predicate of the subject, meaning: "those who call His servants to worship them," and then ﴿they seek﴾ (yabtaghuna) would be in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (ḥal).

Ibn Masʿud read ﴿you call upon﴾ (tadʿuna) with the second-person form (al-fawqiyyah), addressing the audience directly.

The rest read it with the third-person form (al-taḥtiyyah), as a report. There is no disagreement that ﴿they seek﴾ (yabtaghuna) is in the third-person form. The wasilah (means of access) is nearness through obedience and worship, meaning they humbly beseech Allah in seeking what brings them closer to their Lord. The pronoun in ﴿their Lord﴾ (rabbihim) refers either to the worshippers or to the objects of worship. ﴿Which of them is nearest﴾ (ayyuhum aqrab) is a subject and predicate.

Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is "which of them is nearest through the means of access to Allah," that is, who draws near to Him by righteous deeds. It is also permissible for it to be a substitute (badal) for the pronoun in ﴿they seek﴾, meaning: "He who is nearest to Him, may He be exalted, seeks the means of access; how then about one who is other than Him?" It was also said that ﴿they seek﴾ (yabtaghuna) is used with the sense of ﴿they strive eagerly﴾ (yaḥrisuna), meaning: "they strive eagerly, each of them, to be nearest to Him, glorified is He, through obedience and worship, and they hope for His mercy as others hope for it, and they fear His punishment as others fear it." ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is something to be feared﴾ is an explanation (taʿlil) of His saying "they fear His punishment," meaning: His punishment, glorified is He, is truly deserving that the servants, including the angels, the prophets and others, should beware of it.

Then He, glorified is He, showed the end of this world and its people, so He said: ﴿And there is not a city but We will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection﴾. Here ﴿in﴾ (in) is a negative particle, and ﴿there is not﴾ (min) is for totality (li-l-istighraq), meaning: there is no city, whatever city it may be, of the cities of the disbelievers.

Al-Zajjaj said: That is, there is no people of any city but that they will be destroyed, either by death or by a punishment that will uproot them. Thus "city" here means its inhabitants. The phrase ﴿before the Day of Resurrection﴾ was used because destruction on the Day of Resurrection is not restricted to the disbelieving cities but applies to every city, when the lifespan of this world ends. It was also said that destruction is for the righteous cities and punishment for the wicked ones, but the first view is better, because of His saying: ﴿We never destroyed a city except that its people were wrongdoers﴾. ﴿That﴾ (dhalika), the destruction and punishment just mentioned, ﴿was in the Book﴾, that is, the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz), ﴿inscribed﴾ (mastur), that is, written. The word ﴿line﴾ (saṭr) means a line, and in origin it is a verbal noun; the form saṭr with a vowel is similar to it.

Jarir said:

*Whoever wishes, I will sell him my wealth and my finest possessions,*
*Which would not fill, in its ledger, a single line of the Taym.*

The word ﴿finest possessions﴾ (khilʿah) with a dammah on the kha means the best of wealth. The word saṭr is pluralised as asṭar, and the plural of saṭr with a sukun is asṭur.

﴿And nothing prevented Us from sending the signs except that the earlier peoples denied them﴾. The exegetes said: "The people of Makkah asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to turn Safa into gold for them and to remove the mountains of Makkah from around them. Jibril came to him and said: If you wish, what your people asked will be done for them; but if they do not believe, they will not be given respite. If you wish, you may delay them. So Allah revealed this verse."

The meaning is: nothing prevented Us from sending the signs they asked for except the denial of the earlier peoples. If We sent them and these people denied them, they would be hastened to punishment and would not be given respite, as is the way of Allah, glorified is He, with His servants. So the prevention is used metaphorically for abandonment (tark), and the exception is an exception from the most general category (istithna' mufarragh min a'amm al-ashya'), meaning: We did not abandon sending them for any reason except the denial of the earlier peoples. If these people deny them as those did, because they share in disbelief and obstinacy, what befell those will befall them. The first ﴿that﴾ (an) is in the accusative position, as the object of the prevention placed upon it, and the second ﴿that﴾ (an) is in the nominative position. The letter ﴿with﴾ (bi) in ﴿with the signs﴾ (bi-al-ayat) is superfluous (za'idah).

The conclusion is that the thing preventing the sending of the signs they proposed is that proposing them along with denial necessitates total destruction, which is uprooting. We have resolved to delay the affair of those to whom Muhammad (ﷺ) was sent until the Day of Resurrection. It was also said that the meaning of the verse is: these disbelievers, from Quraysh and others like them, are imitators of their fathers, so they will never believe, just as those did not believe; thus sending the signs would be wasted. Then He, glorified is He, cited as evidence for what was mentioned the story of Salih and his she-camel. When they proposed to him what they proposed, namely the she-camel and its description, which has been explained in another place, and Allah gave them what they proposed, but they did not believe, they were utterly destroyed by punishment. The people of Salih were singled out for citation because the traces of their destruction are near in the lands of the Arabs, close to Quraysh and their like, and their travellers and passers-by can see them. So He said: ﴿And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign﴾, meaning a sign possessing sight that people perceive with their eyes, like His saying: ﴿And We made the sign of the day to be visible﴾. Or the state of one who sees it is attributed to it metaphorically, or (p-٨٣٠) it made them people of sight, from "abṣarahu," meaning "he made him perceptive."

It is also read in the passive form (ṣighat al-mafʿul). It is also read with a fatḥah on the mim and the ṣad, in which case it is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause. It is also read with the nominative, as the predicate of an omitted subject, and the sentence is conjoined to an omitted element demanded by the context of the speech, meaning: "So they denied it, and We gave Thamud the she-camel." The meaning of ﴿they wronged themselves through it﴾ (fa-zalamu biha) is that they wronged themselves by denying it. Or ﴿they wronged﴾ (zalamu) is taken to include the sense of "they rejected" or "they disbelieved," meaning: they rejected it or disbelieved in it as wrongdoers, and they did not stop at mere disbelief or rejection.

﴿And We send the signs only as a warning﴾. The interpretation of "the signs" is disputed in several ways. The first is that they are the lessons and miracles which Allah placed at the hands of the messengers as signs of warning, a frightening measure for those who deny. The second is that they are signs of retribution, a warning against sins. The third is the changing of conditions from infancy to youth, then to middle age, then to old age, so that a person may take heed of the changing of his conditions and fear the outcome of his affair. The fourth is the signs of the Qur'an. The fifth is a devastating death. What fits the context is that the signs mentioned are interpreted as the signs that were proposed, meaning: We send the proposed signs only as a warning of the descent of punishment; if they do not fear, it befalls them.

The sentence is independent and has no place in the grammar (la mahalla laha), though it is permissible for it to be in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause from the pronoun in ﴿they wronged themselves through it﴾, meaning: "they wronged themselves through it and did not fear." The circumstance is that We send only ﴿as a warning﴾ (takhwifan), with ﴿the signs﴾ among its kind.

Ibn Qutaybah said: "And We send the proposed signs only as a warning of the descent of immediate punishment."

When He, glorified is He, mentioned the refraining from sending the proposed signs to His Messenger because of the preventing factor mentioned, He strengthened his heart with the promise of victory and triumph, so He said: ﴿And when We said to you: Indeed your Lord has encompassed the people﴾. The adverbial phrase (al-ẓarf) is connected to an omitted verb, meaning: "Remember when We said to you," that is, they are in His grip and under His power, so there is no way for them to escape from what He intends for them, since He encompasses them with His knowledge and power. It was also said that by "the people" are meant the people of Makkah, and His encompassing them means His destroying them, that is, Allah will destroy them. The past tense is used to indicate the certainty of its occurrence, as happened on the day of Badr and the day of the Conquest. It was also said that the meaning is that He, glorified is He, protected him from the people, so that they could not kill him until he conveyed the message of his Lord.

﴿And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people﴾. When He, glorified is He, explained that the sending of signs includes a warning, He added to it the mention of the sign of the Night Journey, which is mentioned at the beginning of the surah, and He called it a "vision" (ru'ya) because it took place at night, or because the disbelievers said: "Perhaps it was only a vision." We have already mentioned at the beginning of the surah another interpretation of this vision. The trial was the apostasy of a people who had embraced Islam when the Prophet (ﷺ) informed them that he had been taken on the Night Journey. It was also said that it was a vision seen in sleep, in which the Prophet (ﷺ) saw that he would enter Makkah, and the Muslims were tested by this. When Allah conquered Makkah, the saying of the Most High was revealed: ﴿Allah has indeed confirmed to His Messenger the vision in truth﴾. This has been objected to, on the grounds that this verse is Meccan, and the vision mentioned occurred in Madinah. It was also said that the vision mentioned in this verse was that he saw the Banu Marwan climbing his pulpit like monkeys, which distressed him, and it was said to him: "It is only the world which they have been given," and so he was comforted. But this is weak, for there is no trial for people in this vision unless the "people" means the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) alone, and the trial means the distress that befell the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), or it is interpreted to mean that he had already informed people of it and they were tested.

It was also said that Allah, glorified is He, showed him in a dream the places where the Quraysh would fall, to the extent that he said: "By Allah, it is as if I am looking at the places where the people will fall," and he pointed to the ground and said: "This is the place where so-and-so will fall, this is the place where so-and-so will fall." When Quraysh heard this, they made his vision a subject of mockery.

﴿And the accursed tree in the Qur'an﴾ is coordinated (ʿatf) with "the vision." It was said that there is inversion and reordering in the speech, and the intended meaning is: "We did not make the vision which We showed you, nor the accursed tree in the Qur'an, except as a trial for the people."

The majority of the exegetes said that it is the tree of al-Zaqqum, and the cursing of it means the cursing of those who eat it, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Indeed the tree of al-Zaqqum is the food of the sinful﴾.

Al-Zajjaj said: The Arabs call every disagreeable food "accursed" (malʿun). The trial in it is that Abu Jahl and others said: "Your companion claims that the Fire of Hell burns stones, and then he says that trees grow in it." So Allah revealed this verse.

It is narrated that Abu Jahl ordered a slave girl, who brought dates and butter, and said to his companions: "Eat it all up (tazaqqamu)!"

Ibn al-Zaba'ra said: "May Allah increase az-Zaqqum in your homes, for it is dates with butter in the language of Yemen." It was also said that the accursed tree is the tree that twines around other trees and kills them, which is the dodder plant (kushuth). It was also said that it is Satan, or the Jews, or the Banu Umayyah.

﴿And We warn them, but it only increases them in great transgression﴾. That is, We warn them with the signs, but the warning only increases them in transgression exceeding all limits, extending to the utmost extremity of defiance. Sending the signs therefore does nothing for them except to increase them in disbelief. At that point We will do to them what We did to those disbelievers before them, namely the punishment of uprooting, but We have decreed the delay of the punishment.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Saʿid ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, al-Bukhari, al-Nasai, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Nuʿaym in al-Dala'il (the Proofs of Prophethood) have related from Ibn Masʿud, concerning His saying: ﴿Say: Call upon those you claim besides Him, and they have no power to remove the harm from you, nor any change﴾, that he said: "A group of humans used to worship a group of jinn. Then the jinn group embraced Islam, but the humans clung to their worship of them. So Allah revealed: ﴿Those whom they call upon, they seek the means of access to their Lord﴾." Both verbs are read with the third-person form (al-taḥtiyyah). Something similar is narrated from Ibn Masʿud through other chains.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh have related from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning the verse, that he said: "The polytheists used to worship the angels, the Messiah and ʿUzayr."

Also narrated from him by another route, with the wording: "Jesus and his mother and Uzayr."

Also narrated from him by another route, with the wording: "They are Jesus and Uzayr, and the sun and the moon."

Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Ask Allah for al-Wasila (the means of nearness) for me." They said: "And what is al-Wasila?" He said: "Nearness to Allah." Then he recited: ﴿They seek the means of access to their Lord, [each of them] which of them is nearest﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibrahim al-Taymi regarding His words ﴿That was written in the Book, inscribed﴾, that he said: "In the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz)."

Ahmad, al-Nasa'i, al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il, and al-Diya' in al-Mukhtara narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The people of Makkah asked the Prophet (ﷺ) to turn al-Safa into gold for them and to remove the mountains from them so that they could farm. It was said to him: 'If you wish, we will give time to them, and if you wish, we will give them what they asked for; but if they disbelieve, they will be destroyed as I destroyed the nations before them.' He said: 'No, rather I will give them time.' So Allah revealed: ﴿And We did not refrain from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them﴾, the verse."

Ahmad and al-Bayhaqi narrated from him by another route something similar.

Al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il narrated from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, who said: "The people said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): 'If only you would bring us a sign like the one Salih and the Prophets brought!' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'If you wish, I will call on Allah and He will send it down upon you; but if you disobey, you will be destroyed.' They said: 'We do not want it.'"

Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh in al-Azama narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿And We do not send the signs except as a warning﴾, that he said: "Death."

Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ahmad in al-Zuhd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from al-Hasan, who said: "It is sudden death (al-mawt al-dhari')."

Ibn Abi Shayba, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Hasan regarding His words ﴿And when We said to you, "Indeed your Lord has encompassed the people"﴾, that he said: "He protected you from the people."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Mujahid regarding the verse, that he said: "They are within His grip."

Abd al-Razzaq, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ahmad, al-Bukhari, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His words ﴿And We did not make the vision﴾, the verse, that he said: "It is a vision of the eye that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was shown on the night he was taken to Bayt al-Maqdis, and it is not a dream vision." ﴿And the cursed tree in the Qur'an﴾, he said: "It is the tree of al-Zaqqum."

Abu Sa'id, Abu Ya'la and Ibn Asakir narrated from Umm Hani that "when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was taken on the Night Journey, he woke up and told some men of Quraysh, while they were mocking him. They asked him for a sign, so he described Bayt al-Maqdis to them and mentioned to them the story of the caravan. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughira said: 'This is a sorcerer.' So Allah revealed to him: ﴿And We did not make the vision﴾," the verse.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Sahl ibn Sa'd, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw the Banu Fulan leaping upon his pulpit like monkeys, and that distressed him, and he was never seen laughing again until he died. So Allah revealed: ﴿And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people﴾."

Ibn Kathir, after citing its chain, said: "This chain is extremely weak. He mentioned among the men of the chain Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Zabban, who is abandoned (matruk), and his shaykh Abd al-Muhaymin ibn Abbas ibn Sahl ibn Sa'd, who is extremely weak."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Amr that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I saw the sons of al-Hakam ibn Abi al-As on the pulpits like monkeys, so Allah revealed: ﴿And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people and the cursed tree﴾," meaning al-Hakam and his offspring.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ya'la ibn Murra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I saw the Banu Umayya on the pulpits of the earth, and they will rule over you, and you will find them to be lords of evil." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was concerned about that, so Allah revealed the verse.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from al-Husayn ibn Ali something similar, raised (marfu'), but it is mursal (its chain lacks a Companion).

Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi and Ibn Asakir narrated from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib something similar, and it is mursal.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Aisha that she said to Marwan ibn al-Hakam: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say to your father and your grandfather: 'You are the cursed tree in the Qur'an.'" In this there is an oddity (nakara) in her words "he said to your father and your grandfather," and perhaps the grandfather of Marwan did not live to the time of prophethood.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, that he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was shown that he, and his companions, entered Makkah, while he was at that time in Madina. He set out for Makkah before the appointed time, and the polytheists turned him back. Some people said: 'He has been turned back, and he had told us that he would enter it.' So his return became a trial for them." These narrations conflict and it is not possible to reconcile them, so the obligation is to resort to preponderance (tarjih), and the more preponderant in number and soundness is that the occasion of revelation of this verse is the story of the Night Journey, so that is what is determined.

Ibn Kathir has related the consensus (ijma') of the authoritative scholars of interpretation on this regarding the vision, and regarding the interpretation of the tree, that it is the tree of al-Zaqqum, so no weight is given to anyone else alongside them.

Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Jahl said, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mentioned the tree of al-Zaqqum as a warning to them: "O assembly of Quraysh, do you know what the tree of al-Zaqqum is with which Muhammad frightens you?" They said: "No." He said: "Dates of Yathrib with butter. By Allah, if we gain control of it, we will devour it completely." Allah the Glorified said: ﴿Indeed, the tree of al-Zaqqum, the food of the sinful﴾ [al-Dukhan: 43–44]. And He revealed: ﴿And the cursed tree in the Qur'an﴾, the verse.

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him regarding His words ﴿And the cursed tree﴾, that he said: "Cursed, because He said: ﴿its shoots are like the heads of devils﴾ [al-Saffat: 65], and the devils are cursed."

**Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 17, verses 56–60 (part 1 of 2):**

.

His saying: ﴿Say: Call upon those you claim besides Him﴾. This is a refutation of a group of the polytheists who worshipped images that they believed to be representations of the angels, and of a group of the People of the Book who said that ʿIsa (Jesus), Maryam (Mary) and ʿUzayr (Ezra) were divine. Allah, glorified is He, commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to say to them: "Call upon those you claim are gods besides Allah." It was also said that by "those you claim" He meant a company of jinn whom some of the Arabs claimed to be with them. The verse is restricted to those mentioned earlier because of His saying: ﴿They seek the means of access to their Lord﴾, for this does not befit inanimate objects. ﴿Then they have no power to remove the harm from you﴾, meaning they are not able to do so. The true object of worship is the one who has the power to remove harm and to change one state into another and one place into another. It is therefore necessary to conclude with certainty that what you claim to be gods are not gods.

Then, glorified is He, emphasised their lack of power by showing the extent of their need for Allah in bringing benefits and warding off harms, so He said: ﴿Those whom they call upon, they seek the means of access to their Lord﴾. Here ﴿those﴾ (ulaʾika) is the subject (mubtadaʾ), and ﴿whom they call upon﴾ (alladhina yadʿuna) is its qualifying clause (ṣifa), with the relative pronoun (ḍamir al-ṣila) omitted, meaning "whom they call upon." The predicate of the subject is ﴿they seek the means of access to their Lord﴾ (yabtaghuna ila rabbihimu al-wasilah). It is also permissible for ﴿whom they call upon﴾ (alladhina yadʿuna) to be the predicate of the subject, meaning: "those who call His servants to worship them," and then ﴿they seek﴾ (yabtaghuna) would be in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (ḥal).

Ibn Masʿud read ﴿you call upon﴾ (tadʿuna) with the second-person form (al-fawqiyyah), addressing the audience directly.

The rest read it with the third-person form (al-taḥtiyyah), as a report. There is no disagreement that ﴿they seek﴾ (yabtaghuna) is in the third-person form. The wasilah (means of access) is nearness through obedience and worship, meaning they humbly beseech Allah in seeking what brings them closer to their Lord. The pronoun in ﴿their Lord﴾ (rabbihim) refers either to the worshippers or to the objects of worship. ﴿Which of them is nearest﴾ (ayyuhum aqrab) is a subject and predicate.

Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is "which of them is nearest through the means of access to Allah," that is, who draws near to Him by righteous deeds. It is also permissible for it to be a substitute (badal) for the pronoun in ﴿they seek﴾, meaning: "He who is nearest to Him, may He be exalted, seeks the means of access; how then about one who is other than Him?" It was also said that ﴿they seek﴾ (yabtaghuna) is used with the sense of ﴿they strive eagerly﴾ (yaḥrisuna), meaning: "they strive eagerly, each of them, to be nearest to Him, glorified is He, through obedience and worship, and they hope for His mercy as others hope for it, and they fear His punishment as others fear it." ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is something to be feared﴾ is an explanation (taʿlil) of His saying "they fear His punishment," meaning: His punishment, glorified is He, is truly deserving that the servants, including the angels, the prophets and others, should beware of it.

Then He, glorified is He, showed the end of this world and its people, so He said: ﴿And there is not a city but We will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection﴾. Here ﴿in﴾ (in) is a negative particle, and ﴿there is not﴾ (min) is for totality (li-l-istighraq), meaning: there is no city, whatever city it may be, of the cities of the disbelievers.

Al-Zajjaj said: That is, there is no people of any city but that they will be destroyed, either by death or by a punishment that will uproot them. Thus "city" here means its inhabitants. The phrase ﴿before the Day of Resurrection﴾ was used because destruction on the Day of Resurrection is not restricted to the disbelieving cities but applies to every city, when the lifespan of this world ends. It was also said that destruction is for the righteous cities and punishment for the wicked ones, but the first view is better, because of His saying: ﴿We never destroyed a city except that its people were wrongdoers﴾. ﴿That﴾ (dhalika), the destruction and punishment just mentioned, ﴿was in the Book﴾, that is, the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz), ﴿inscribed﴾ (mastur), that is, written. The word ﴿line﴾ (saṭr) means a line, and in origin it is a verbal noun; the form saṭr with a vowel is similar to it.

Jarir said:

*Whoever wishes, I will sell him my wealth and my finest possessions,*
*Which would not fill, in its ledger, a single line of the Taym.*

The word ﴿finest possessions﴾ (khilʿah) with a dammah on the kha means the best of wealth. The word saṭr is pluralised as asṭar, and the plural of saṭr with a sukun is asṭur.

﴿And nothing prevented Us from sending the signs except that the earlier peoples denied them﴾. The exegetes said: "The people of Makkah asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to turn Safa into gold for them and to remove the mountains of Makkah from around them. Jibril came to him and said: If you wish, what your people asked will be done for them; but if they do not believe, they will not be given respite. If you wish, you may delay them. So Allah revealed this verse."

The meaning is: nothing prevented Us from sending the signs they asked for except the denial of the earlier peoples. If We sent them and these people denied them, they would be hastened to punishment and would not be given respite, as is the way of Allah, glorified is He, with His servants. So the prevention is used metaphorically for abandonment (tark), and the exception is an exception from the most general category (istithna' mufarragh min a'amm al-ashya'), meaning: We did not abandon sending them for any reason except the denial of the earlier peoples. If these people deny them as those did, because they share in disbelief and obstinacy, what befell those will befall them. The first ﴿that﴾ (an) is in the accusative position, as the object of the prevention placed upon it, and the second ﴿that﴾ (an) is in the nominative position. The letter ﴿with﴾ (bi) in ﴿with the signs﴾ (bi-al-ayat) is superfluous (za'idah).

The conclusion is that the thing preventing the sending of the signs they proposed is that proposing them along with denial necessitates total destruction, which is uprooting. We have resolved to delay the affair of those to whom Muhammad (ﷺ) was sent until the Day of Resurrection. It was also said that the meaning of the verse is: these disbelievers, from Quraysh and others like them, are imitators of their fathers, so they will never believe, just as those did not believe; thus sending the signs would be wasted. Then He, glorified is He, cited as evidence for what was mentioned the story of Salih and his she-camel. When they proposed to him what they proposed, namely the she-camel and its description, which has been explained in another place, and Allah gave them what they proposed, but they did not believe, they were utterly destroyed by punishment. The people of Salih were singled out for citation because the traces of their destruction are near in the lands of the Arabs, close to Quraysh and their like, and their travellers and passers-by can see them. So He said: ﴿And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign﴾, meaning a sign possessing sight that people perceive with their eyes, like His saying: ﴿And We made the sign of the day to be visible﴾. Or the state of one who sees it is attributed to it metaphorically, or (p-٨٣٠) it made them people of sight, from "abṣarahu," meaning "he made him perceptive."

It is also read in the passive form (ṣighat al-mafʿul). It is also read with a fatḥah on the mim and the ṣad, in which case it is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause. It is also read with the nominative, as the predicate of an omitted subject, and the sentence is conjoined to an omitted element demanded by the context of the speech, meaning: "So they denied it, and We gave Thamud the she-camel." The meaning of ﴿they wronged themselves through it﴾ (fa-zalamu biha) is that they wronged themselves by denying it. Or ﴿they wronged﴾ (zalamu) is taken to include the sense of "they rejected" or "they disbelieved," meaning: they rejected it or disbelieved in it as wrongdoers, and they did not stop at mere disbelief or rejection.

﴿And We send the signs only as a warning﴾. The interpretation of "the signs" is disputed in several ways. The first is that they are the lessons and miracles which Allah placed at the hands of the messengers as signs of warning, a frightening measure for those who deny. The second is that they are signs of retribution, a warning against sins. The third is the changing of conditions from infancy to youth, then to middle age, then to old age, so that a person may take heed of the changing of his conditions and fear the outcome of his affair. The fourth is the signs of the Qur'an. The fifth is a devastating death. What fits the context is that the signs mentioned are interpreted as the signs that were proposed, meaning: We send the proposed signs only as a warning of the descent of punishment; if they do not fear, it befalls them.

The sentence is independent and has no place in the grammar (la mahalla laha), though it is permissible for it to be in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause from the pronoun in ﴿they wronged themselves through it﴾, meaning: "they wronged themselves through it and did not fear." The circumstance is that We send only ﴿as a warning﴾ (takhwifan), with ﴿the signs﴾ among its kind.

Ibn Qutaybah said: "And We send the proposed signs only as a warning of the descent of immediate punishment."

When He, glorified is He, mentioned the refraining from sending the proposed signs to His Messenger because of the preventing factor mentioned, He strengthened his heart with the promise of victory and triumph, so He said: ﴿And when We said to you: Indeed your Lord has encompassed the people﴾. The adverbial phrase (al-ẓarf) is connected to an omitted verb, meaning: "Remember when We said to you," that is, they are in His grip and under His power, so there is no way for them to escape from what He intends for them, since He encompasses them with His knowledge and power. It was also said that by "the people" are meant the people of Makkah, and His encompassing them means His destroying them, that is, Allah will destroy them. The past tense is used to indicate the certainty of its occurrence, as happened on the day of Badr and the day of the Conquest. It was also said that the meaning is that He, glorified is He, protected him from the people, so that they could not kill him until he conveyed the message of his Lord.

﴿And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people﴾. When He, glorified is He, explained that the sending of signs includes a warning, He added to it the mention of the sign of the Night Journey, which is mentioned at the beginning of the surah, and He called it a "vision" (ru'ya) because it took place at night, or because the disbelievers said: "Perhaps it was only a vision." We have already mentioned at the beginning of the surah another interpretation of this vision. The trial was the apostasy of a people who had embraced Islam when the Prophet (ﷺ) informed them that he had been taken on the Night Journey. It was also said that it was a vision seen in sleep, in which the Prophet (ﷺ) saw that he would enter Makkah, and the Muslims were tested by this. When Allah conquered Makkah, the saying of the Most High was revealed: ﴿Allah has indeed confirmed to His Messenger the vision in truth﴾. This has been objected to, on the grounds that this verse is Meccan, and the vision mentioned occurred in Madinah. It was also said that the vision mentioned in this verse was that he saw the Banu Marwan climbing his pulpit like monkeys, which distressed him, and it was said to him: "It is only the world which they have been given," and so he was comforted. But this is weak, for there is no trial for people in this vision unless the "people" means the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) alone, and the trial means the distress that befell the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), or it is interpreted to mean that he had already informed people of it and they were tested.

It was also said that Allah, glorified is He, showed him in a dream the places where the Quraysh would fall, to the extent that he said: "By Allah, it is as if I am looking at the places where the people will fall," and he pointed to the ground and said: "This is the place where so-and-so will fall, this is the place where so-and-so will fall." When Quraysh heard this, they made his vision a subject of mockery.

﴿And the accursed tree in the Qur'an﴾ is coordinated (ʿatf) with "the vision." It was said that there is inversion and reordering in the speech, and the intended meaning is: "We did not make the vision which We showed you, nor the accursed tree in the Qur'an, except as a trial for the people."

The majority of the exegetes said that it is the tree of al-Zaqqum, and the cursing of it means the cursing of those who eat it, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Indeed the tree of al-Zaqqum is the food of the sinful﴾.

Al-Zajjaj said: The Arabs call every disagreeable food "accursed" (malʿun). The trial in it is that Abu Jahl and others said: "Your companion claims that the Fire of Hell burns stones, and then he says that trees grow in it." So Allah revealed this verse.

It is narrated that Abu Jahl ordered a slave girl, who brought dates and butter, and said to his companions: "Eat it all up (tazaqqamu)!"

Ibn al-Zaba'ra said: "May Allah increase az-Zaqqum in your homes, for it is dates with butter in the language of Yemen." It was also said that the accursed tree is the tree that twines around other trees and kills them, which is the dodder plant (kushuth). It was also said that it is Satan, or the Jews, or the Banu Umayyah.

﴿And We warn them, but it only increases them in great transgression﴾. That is, We warn them with the signs, but the warning only increases them in transgression exceeding all limits, extending to the utmost extremity of defiance. Sending the signs therefore does nothing for them except to increase them in disbelief. At that point We will do to them what We did to those disbelievers before them, namely the punishment of uprooting, but We have decreed the delay of the punishment.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Saʿid ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, al-Bukhari, al-Nasai, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Nuʿaym in al-Dala'il (the Proofs of Prophethood) have related from Ibn Masʿud, concerning His saying: ﴿Say: Call upon those you claim besides Him, and they have no power to remove the harm from you, nor any change﴾, that he said: "A group of humans used to worship a group of jinn. Then the jinn group embraced Islam, but the humans clung to their worship of them. So Allah revealed: ﴿Those whom they call upon, they seek the means of access to their Lord﴾." Both verbs are read with the third-person form (al-taḥtiyyah). Something similar is narrated from Ibn Masʿud through other chains.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh have related from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning the verse, that he said: "The polytheists used to worship the angels, the Messiah and ʿUzayr."

Also narrated from him by another route, with the wording: "Jesus and his mother and Uzayr."

Also narrated from him by another route, with the wording: "They are Jesus and Uzayr, and the sun and the moon."

Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Ask Allah for al-Wasila (the means of nearness) for me." They said: "And what is al-Wasila?" He said: "Nearness to Allah." Then he recited: ﴿They seek the means of access to their Lord, [each of them] which of them is nearest﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibrahim al-Taymi regarding His words ﴿That was written in the Book, inscribed﴾, that he said: "In the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz)."

Ahmad, al-Nasa'i, al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il, and al-Diya' in al-Mukhtara narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The people of Makkah asked the Prophet (ﷺ) to turn al-Safa into gold for them and to remove the mountains from them so that they could farm. It was said to him: 'If you wish, we will give time to them, and if you wish, we will give them what they asked for; but if they disbelieve, they will be destroyed as I destroyed the nations before them.' He said: 'No, rather I will give them time.' So Allah revealed: ﴿And We did not refrain from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them﴾, the verse."

Ahmad and al-Bayhaqi narrated from him by another route something similar.

Al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il narrated from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, who said: "The people said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): 'If only you would bring us a sign like the one Salih and the Prophets brought!' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'If you wish, I will call on Allah and He will send it down upon you; but if you disobey, you will be destroyed.' They said: 'We do not want it.'"

Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh in al-Azama narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿And We do not send the signs except as a warning﴾, that he said: "Death."

Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ahmad in al-Zuhd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from al-Hasan, who said: "It is sudden death (al-mawt al-dhari')."

Ibn Abi Shayba, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Hasan regarding His words ﴿And when We said to you, "Indeed your Lord has encompassed the people"﴾, that he said: "He protected you from the people."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Mujahid regarding the verse, that he said: "They are within His grip."

Abd al-Razzaq, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ahmad, al-Bukhari, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His words ﴿And We did not make the vision﴾, the verse, that he said: "It is a vision of the eye that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was shown on the night he was taken to Bayt al-Maqdis, and it is not a dream vision." ﴿And the cursed tree in the Qur'an﴾, he said: "It is the tree of al-Zaqqum."

Abu Sa'id, Abu Ya'la and Ibn Asakir narrated from Umm Hani that "when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was taken on the Night Journey, he woke up and told some men of Quraysh, while they were mocking him. They asked him for a sign, so he described Bayt al-Maqdis to them and mentioned to them the story of the caravan. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughira said: 'This is a sorcerer.' So Allah revealed to him: ﴿And We did not make the vision﴾," the verse.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Sahl ibn Sa'd, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw the Banu Fulan leaping upon his pulpit like monkeys, and that distressed him, and he was never seen laughing again until he died. So Allah revealed: ﴿And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people﴾."

Ibn Kathir, after citing its chain, said: "This chain is extremely weak. He mentioned among the men of the chain Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Zabban, who is abandoned (matruk), and his shaykh Abd al-Muhaymin ibn Abbas ibn Sahl ibn Sa'd, who is extremely weak."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Amr that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I saw the sons of al-Hakam ibn Abi al-As on the pulpits like monkeys, so Allah revealed: ﴿And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people and the cursed tree﴾," meaning al-Hakam and his offspring.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ya'la ibn Murra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I saw the Banu Umayya on the pulpits of the earth, and they will rule over you, and you will find them to be lords of evil." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was concerned about that, so Allah revealed the verse.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from al-Husayn ibn Ali something similar, raised (marfu'), but it is mursal (its chain lacks a Companion).

Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi and Ibn Asakir narrated from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib something similar, and it is mursal.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Aisha that she said to Marwan ibn al-Hakam: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say to your father and your grandfather: 'You are the cursed tree in the Qur'an.'" In this there is an oddity (nakara) in her words "he said to your father and your grandfather," and perhaps the grandfather of Marwan did not live to the time of prophethood.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, that he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was shown that he, and his companions, entered Makkah, while he was at that time in Madina. He set out for Makkah before the appointed time, and the polytheists turned him back. Some people said: 'He has been turned back, and he had told us that he would enter it.' So his return became a trial for them." These narrations conflict and it is not possible to reconcile them, so the obligation is to resort to preponderance (tarjih), and the more preponderant in number and soundness is that the occasion of revelation of this verse is the story of the Night Journey, so that is what is determined.

Ibn Kathir has related the consensus (ijma') of the authoritative scholars of interpretation on this regarding the vision, and regarding the interpretation of the tree, that it is the tree of al-Zaqqum, so no weight is given to anyone else alongside them.

Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Jahl said, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mentioned the tree of al-Zaqqum as a warning to them: "O assembly of Quraysh, do you know what the tree of al-Zaqqum is with which Muhammad frightens you?" They said: "No." He said: "Dates of Yathrib with butter. By Allah, if we gain control of it, we will devour it completely." Allah the Glorified said: ﴿Indeed, the tree of al-Zaqqum, the food of the sinful﴾ [al-Dukhan: 43–44]. And He revealed: ﴿And the cursed tree in the Qur'an﴾, the verse.

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him regarding His words ﴿And the cursed tree﴾, that he said: "Cursed, because He said: ﴿its shoots are like the heads of devils﴾ [al-Saffat: 65], and the devils are cursed."

[p. 832]

When Allah, glorified is He, mentioned that the Messenger (ﷺ) was in great affliction from his people and severe trial, He wished to show that all the prophets were like this, and that this is an ancient practice initiated by the accursed Iblis. Also, when He mentioned that those whom they call upon seek the means (*wasilah*) to their Lord, as to which of them is nearest, and hope for His mercy and fear His punishment, He mentioned here what confirms that, saying: ﴿And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam"﴾. This story Allah, glorified is He, has mentioned in seven places: in al-Baqarah, al-A'raf, al-Hijr, this surah, al-Kahf, Ta-Ha, and Sad. Its tafsir has already been explained at length, so here we shall limit ourselves to explaining the words that have not previously been mentioned. His saying *tinan* (from clay) is in the accusative by the removal of the preposition (*naz' al-khafid*), i.e., "from clay," or it is in the accusative of circumstance (*hal*). [p. 832]

Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is "to one whom You created from clay," and it is in the accusative of circumstance.

﴿Tell me﴾, i.e., inform me about this one whom You have preferred over me, why You preferred him? ﴿You created me from fire and You created him from clay﴾ [al-A'raf: 12]. Here the object has been omitted because it is known. ﴿I will surely seize his descendants﴾, i.e., I will surely gain control over them through misguidance and leading astray. Al-Wahidi said: its origin is from *ihtinak al-jarad al-zar'* (the locusts' seizing of the crops), which is to uproot it with their jaws and corrupt it. This is the original meaning; then gaining control over a thing and taking all of it was called *ihtinak*. It was also said: its meaning is "I will drive them wherever I wish, and lead them wherever I want," from the phrase *hannaktu al-faras uhannikuhu hanka*, when one puts the halter in the horse's mouth. The first meaning is more suitable to the sense of this verse, and from it is the saying of the poet:

"I complain to you of a year that has overwhelmed us with hardship upon hardship, and has struck us down,
and has seized our wealth and dispersed it."

That is: it uprooted our wealth. The *lam* in ﴿Certainly, if You give me respite﴾ is the *lam* of preparation (*al-muwatti'ah*). The accursed one swore this oath that he would do to the descendants of Adam what he mentioned, either because of a knowledge he had already obtained through an overheard report that he had stolen, or he said it because of what he assumed about the strength of the effect of his plotting upon the children of Adam, and that it flows through them along the channels of the blood, and that they are such that his plotting prevails among them and his whispering is accepted by them, except those whom Allah protects; and these are the ones intended by His saying ﴿except a few﴾. The meaning of this exception is in His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them﴾. What we have mentioned is supported by His, exalted is He, saying: ﴿And Iblis had already confirmed his assumption about them﴾ [Saba': 20]. It indicates that he said what he said here relying on assumption. It was also said that he inferred this from the saying of the angels: ﴿Will You place in it one who causes corruption therein?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 30]. It was also said that he knew this from the nature of humans, because of the desires placed within them, or he assumed this because he had whispered to Adam and he accepted it from him and did not find in him resolve, as is narrated from al-Hasan.

﴿He said, "Go, and whoever follows you among them﴾, i.e., obeys you, ﴿indeed Hell is your recompense﴾, i.e., Iblis and whoever obeys him, ﴿a full recompense﴾, i.e., complete and perfect. It is said: *wafartuhu afiruhu wafran*, and *wafara al-mal bi-nafsihi yafiru wufuran*, so it is *wafir*. It is a verbal noun (*masdar*). From it is the saying of Zuhayr:

"And whoever makes kindness at the expense of his honor, it will be increased for him; and whoever does not guard against insult will be insulted."

Then Allah, glorified is He, repeated the respite to the accursed Iblis, saying: ﴿And incite whomever you can among them with your voice﴾, i.e., provoke and entice whomever you can of the children of Adam. It is said: *afazzahu* and *istafazzahu*, meaning he disturbed him and lured him. The meaning is: lure them with your voice, calling them to disobedience of Allah. It was also said: it is singing, frivolity, play, and flutes. ﴿And rally against them with your horsemen and your footmen﴾. Al-Farra' and Abu 'Ubaydah said: *ajlib* comes from *al-jalabah* and *al-sayah*, i.e., shout against them. [p. 832]

Al-Zajjaj said: i.e., gather against them everything you are capable of of your schemes.

So *al-ijlab* is gathering, and the *ba'* in ﴿with your horsemen﴾ is extra (*za'idah*).

Ibn al-Sikkit said: *al-ijlab* is assistance, and *al-khayl* applies to riders, as in the saying of the Messenger (ﷺ): "O horses of Allah, mount!" and it applies to mares. *Al-rajl*, with the *jim* sukun, is the plural of *rajil* (on foot), like *tajir* and *tajr*, *sahib* and *sahb*. Hafs read it with a *kasrah* on the *jim*, considering it an adjective.

Abu Zayd said: it is said *rajil* and *rajul*, in the sense of *rajil* (on foot). So "horses and foot" is a metaphor for all of Satan's schemes, or what is meant is every rider and every walker in disobedience of Allah. ﴿And share with them in wealth and children﴾. As for sharing in wealth, it is every disposal of it that contravenes the way of the Law, whether taking it without right or placing it in a place without right, like usurpation, theft, and usury. From this is slitting the ears of cattle and making them *bahirah* and *sa'ibah*. Sharing in children is claiming a child without a lawful cause, obtaining them through fornication, naming them *Abd al-Lat* and *Abd al-'Uzza*, and mistreating them in upbringing in a way that they grow accustomed to the qualities of evil and the deeds of wickedness. It includes what they killed of their children out of fear of poverty, the burying alive of daughters, and making their children follow the disbelieving religion they are upon. From this also is the sharing of Satan with one who has intercourse without mentioning the name of Allah. Then He said: ﴿And promise them﴾. Al-Farra' said: say to them, "There is no Paradise and no Fire." [p. 832]

Al-Zajjaj said: he promised them that they will not be resurrected. ﴿But Satan promises them only delusion﴾, i.e., falsehood. The root of *ghurur* is making error appear attractive by that which gives the impression of being correct. It was also said: its meaning is, "Promise them victory over whoever opposes them." Sharing in children is claiming a child without a lawful cause, obtaining them through fornication, naming them *Abd al-Lat* and *Abd al-'Uzza*, and mistreating them in upbringing in a way that they grow accustomed to the qualities of evil and the deeds of wickedness. It includes what they killed of their children out of fear of poverty, the burying alive of daughters, and making their children follow the disbelieving religion they are upon. From this also is the sharing of Satan with one who has intercourse without mentioning the name of Allah. Then He said: ﴿And promise them﴾. Al-Farra' said: say to them, "There is no Paradise and no Fire." [p. 832]

Al-Zajjaj said: he promised them that they will not be resurrected. ﴿But Satan promises them only delusion﴾, i.e., falsehood. The root of *ghurur* is making error appear attractive by that which gives the impression of being correct. It was also said: its meaning is, "Promise them victory over whoever opposes them." These commands to Satan are in the manner of threat and severe warning. It was also said: they are in the manner of belittling him and those who follow him.

﴿Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them﴾: He means His believing servants, as in other places in the Mighty Book, where the attribution of "servants" to Him is intended to mean the believers, because of the honor in the attribution. It was also said: what is intended is all servants, by the evidence of the exception in His saying in another place: ﴿except those who follow you of the misguided﴾ [al-Hijr: 42]. By "authority" is meant domination. ﴿And sufficient is your Lord as a Disposer of affairs﴾, on whom they rely. He is the One who repels from them the plotting of Satan and protects them from his misguidance.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Iblis said, "Adam was created from dust, from clay, he was created weak, and I was created from fire, and fire burns everything." ﴿I will surely seize his descendants, except a few﴾, and so Allah confirmed his assumption about them.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him regarding ﴿I will surely seize his descendants﴾: "I will surely gain control over them."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Mujahid regarding ﴿I will surely seize his descendants﴾: "I will surely encompass them."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Zayd, who said: "I will surely mislead them."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Mujahid regarding *mawfuran* (full): "complete."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And incite whomever you can among them with your voice﴾: "His voice is every caller who calls to disobedience of Allah." ﴿And rally against them with your horsemen﴾: "Every rider in disobedience of Allah." (*And your footmen*): "Every walker in disobedience of Allah." ﴿And share with them in wealth﴾: "Every wealth in disobedience of Allah." (*And children*): "Every child they killed and every unlawful thing they committed concerning them."

Al-Firyabi, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him regarding the verse: "Every horse that goes in disobedience of Allah, every wealth taken without right, and every child of fornication."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding the verse: "(*Wealth*) is what they used to forbid of their cattle; (*and children*) are the children of fornication." [p. 832–833]

Ibn Jarir also narrated from him, who said: "(*Wealth*) is the *bahirah*, *sa'ibah*, and *wasilah* dedicated to other than Allah; (*and children*) they named Abd al-Harith and Abd Shams."

[p. 832]

When Allah, glorified is He, mentioned that the Messenger (ﷺ) was in great affliction from his people and severe trial, He wished to show that all the prophets were like this, and that this is an ancient practice initiated by the accursed Iblis. Also, when He mentioned that those whom they call upon seek the means (*wasilah*) to their Lord, as to which of them is nearest, and hope for His mercy and fear His punishment, He mentioned here what confirms that, saying: ﴿And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam"﴾. This story Allah, glorified is He, has mentioned in seven places: in al-Baqarah, al-A'raf, al-Hijr, this surah, al-Kahf, Ta-Ha, and Sad. Its tafsir has already been explained at length, so here we shall limit ourselves to explaining the words that have not previously been mentioned. His saying *tinan* (from clay) is in the accusative by the removal of the preposition (*naz' al-khafid*), i.e., "from clay," or it is in the accusative of circumstance (*hal*). [p. 832]

Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is "to one whom You created from clay," and it is in the accusative of circumstance.

﴿Tell me﴾, i.e., inform me about this one whom You have preferred over me, why You preferred him? ﴿You created me from fire and You created him from clay﴾ [al-A'raf: 12]. Here the object has been omitted because it is known. ﴿I will surely seize his descendants﴾, i.e., I will surely gain control over them through misguidance and leading astray. Al-Wahidi said: its origin is from *ihtinak al-jarad al-zar'* (the locusts' seizing of the crops), which is to uproot it with their jaws and corrupt it. This is the original meaning; then gaining control over a thing and taking all of it was called *ihtinak*. It was also said: its meaning is "I will drive them wherever I wish, and lead them wherever I want," from the phrase *hannaktu al-faras uhannikuhu hanka*, when one puts the halter in the horse's mouth. The first meaning is more suitable to the sense of this verse, and from it is the saying of the poet:

"I complain to you of a year that has overwhelmed us with hardship upon hardship, and has struck us down,
and has seized our wealth and dispersed it."

That is: it uprooted our wealth. The *lam* in ﴿Certainly, if You give me respite﴾ is the *lam* of preparation (*al-muwatti'ah*). The accursed one swore this oath that he would do to the descendants of Adam what he mentioned, either because of a knowledge he had already obtained through an overheard report that he had stolen, or he said it because of what he assumed about the strength of the effect of his plotting upon the children of Adam, and that it flows through them along the channels of the blood, and that they are such that his plotting prevails among them and his whispering is accepted by them, except those whom Allah protects; and these are the ones intended by His saying ﴿except a few﴾. The meaning of this exception is in His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them﴾. What we have mentioned is supported by His, exalted is He, saying: ﴿And Iblis had already confirmed his assumption about them﴾ [Saba': 20]. It indicates that he said what he said here relying on assumption. It was also said that he inferred this from the saying of the angels: ﴿Will You place in it one who causes corruption therein?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 30]. It was also said that he knew this from the nature of humans, because of the desires placed within them, or he assumed this because he had whispered to Adam and he accepted it from him and did not find in him resolve, as is narrated from al-Hasan.

﴿He said, "Go, and whoever follows you among them﴾, i.e., obeys you, ﴿indeed Hell is your recompense﴾, i.e., Iblis and whoever obeys him, ﴿a full recompense﴾, i.e., complete and perfect. It is said: *wafartuhu afiruhu wafran*, and *wafara al-mal bi-nafsihi yafiru wufuran*, so it is *wafir*. It is a verbal noun (*masdar*). From it is the saying of Zuhayr:

"And whoever makes kindness at the expense of his honor, it will be increased for him; and whoever does not guard against insult will be insulted."

Then Allah, glorified is He, repeated the respite to the accursed Iblis, saying: ﴿And incite whomever you can among them with your voice﴾, i.e., provoke and entice whomever you can of the children of Adam. It is said: *afazzahu* and *istafazzahu*, meaning he disturbed him and lured him. The meaning is: lure them with your voice, calling them to disobedience of Allah. It was also said: it is singing, frivolity, play, and flutes. ﴿And rally against them with your horsemen and your footmen﴾. Al-Farra' and Abu 'Ubaydah said: *ajlib* comes from *al-jalabah* and *al-sayah*, i.e., shout against them. [p. 832]

Al-Zajjaj said: i.e., gather against them everything you are capable of of your schemes.

Hafs read it with a *kasrah* on the *jim*, considering it an adjective.

Abu Zayd said: it is said *rajil* and *rajul*, in the sense of *rajil* (on foot). So "horses and foot" is a metaphor for all of Satan's schemes, or what is meant is every rider and every walker in disobedience of Allah. ﴿And share with them in wealth and children﴾. **Al-Shawkani's commentary (Fath al-Qadir) on Surah 17, verses 66–70:**

His words, ﴿Your Lord is He who drives the ship for you through the sea﴾. *Al-Izja'* (driving, propelling) means to drive, to set in motion, and to make move. From it is His, glorified is He, saying: ﴿Do you not see that Allah drives the clouds﴾ [al-Nur: 43]. And the poet's saying:

*O rider driving his mount, ask the Banu Asad what these images are.*

And another's saying:

*A she-camel driving her young behind her.*

The meaning is that Allah, glorified is He, moves the ships in the sea by means of the wind. *Al-fulk* (ships) here is a plural, as has already been mentioned. *Al-bahr* (the sea) is a large body of water, whether sweet or salty, though this name has become predominantly applied to the salt sea. ﴿That you may seek of His bounty﴾, i.e., of His provision which He has graciously bestowed upon His servants, or of profit through trade. The *min* (of) is either superfluous or partitive. In this verse there is a reminder to them of Allah's blessings upon them, so that they do not worship other than Him or associate anyone with Him. The clause ﴿Indeed, He is ever Merciful to you﴾ is a causal explanation of what preceded it, i.e., He has been merciful to you, so He guided you to the benefits of your worldly life.

﴿And when harm touches you at sea﴾, meaning: the fear of drowning, ﴿those whom you invoke disappear﴾ from among the gods, and pass from your minds. Nothing that you used to invoke besides Him, whether an idol, a jinn, an angel, or a human, is found to rescue you, ﴿except Him alone﴾. You then place your hope in His mercy and rescue. The exception here is *munqati'* (disconnected). The meaning of the verse is that the disbelievers believe about their idols and all their other objects of worship only that they benefit them in circumstances other than this one. In this situation, however, each of them knows by innate nature, with a knowledge he cannot repel, that the idols and the like have no power to act. ﴿But when He brings you safely to land, you turn away﴾ from sincerity to Allah and His oneness, and return to invoking your idols and seeking aid from them. ﴿And man has ever been ungrateful﴾, i.e., greatly ungrateful for the blessing of Allah. This is a causal explanation of what preceded it. The meaning is that in times of hardship they cling to Allah's mercy, and in times of ease they turn away from Him.

Then He, glorified is He, rebuked them for their bad conduct, saying: ﴿Do you feel secure that He will not cause the side of the land to swallow you?﴾ The *hamza* is interrogative for denial, and the *fa'* (then) is conjunctive upon an omitted clause, whose estimated sense is: "Have you been delivered, and so you felt secure, and this led you to turn away?" Thus He made clear to them that He is able to destroy them on land, even if they are saved from the sea.

*Al-khasf* (swallowing) is when the earth collapses upon something. It is said: *bi'r khasif* (a well that is caved in) when its base has collapsed; *ayn khasif* (a sunken eye) means one whose pupil is sunk deep in the head; *khasafat 'ayn al-ma'* (the spring of water sank) when its water has receded; and *khasafat al-shams* (the sun was eclipsed) when it set out of sight of the earth. *Janib al-barr* (the side of the land) means the region of the earth. He called it "side" because after the swallowing it becomes a side; and also because the sea is a side of the earth and the land is a side.

It has been said that they were on the sea shore, and its shore is the side of the land, so they felt secure there from the dangers of the sea. Thus He warned them of what they felt secure from on land, just as He warned them of what they feared from the sea.

﴿Or send upon you a violent wind of stones﴾. Abu 'Ubayda and al-Qutaybi said: *al-Hasb* means throwing, i.e., a violent wind that casts [stones], namely a wind that hurls small pebbles. Al-Zajjaj said: *al-Hasib* is dust in which there are pebbles, so *al-hasib* is that which has pebbles, like *laabin* (milky) and *tamir* (dated). It has been said: *al-hasib* is stones from the sky that pelt them, as was done to the people of Lot. The cloud that throws hail is also called *hasib*, and from this is al-Farazdaq's saying:

*Facing the mountains of Syria, they strike us with a hail like scattered cotton-carding.*

﴿Then you will not find for yourselves any protector﴾, i.e., a guardian and helper who would protect you from the might of Allah.

﴿Or do you feel secure that He will not return you to it another time﴾, i.e., to the sea again, by stirring up your motives and multiplying your needs to ride it. He used *fi* (in) rather than saying *ila* (to) the sea, to indicate their settling in it. ﴿Then send upon you a violent wind of storm﴾. *Al-qasif* is the strong wind that breaks forcefully, from *qasafa al-shay'* (he broke the thing forcefully), meaning he broke it violently; *al-qasf* is breaking. Or it is the wind that has a *qasif*, i.e., a loud sound, from their saying: "a thundering thunder" (*ra'd qasif*), meaning very loud. ﴿And drown you﴾. Abu Ja'far, Shayba, Ruways and Mujahid read *fa-tughriqakum* (with a *ta'* at the beginning), with the wind as its subject. Al-Hasan, Qatada and Ibn Wardan read *fa-yughriqakum* with a *ya'* and with shadda on the *ra'*. Abu Ja'far also read *al-riyah* (the winds). Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read with *nun* (we) in all these verbs.

The rest read with *ya'* in all of them as well. The *ba'* in ﴿because you disbelieved﴾ denotes causation, i.e., because of your disbelief. ﴿Then you will not find for yourselves against Us any avenger for it﴾, i.e., a pursuer who would demand from us what we have done. Al-Zajjaj said: you will not find anyone to follow us in denouncing what has befallen you. Al-Nahhas said: it is from *al-tha'r* (vengeance), and so it is said of anyone who seeks vengeance or other things: *tabi'* and *tabi'* (a pursuer).

﴿And We have certainly honoured the children of Adam﴾. This is a general statement mentioning the blessing that Allah has bestowed upon the children of Adam, i.e., We have honoured them all. This honour includes that He created them in this good form and singled them out with what He has specifically granted them of foods, drinks and clothing, in a manner that none of the other kinds of animals possesses the like of.

Ibn Jarir relates from a group that this honour is that they eat with their hands, while the other animals eat with the mouth; al-Nahhas relates it similarly. It has been said: He distinguished them with speech, intellect and discernment. It has been said: He honoured men with beards and women with long hair. Ibn Jarir said: He honoured them by giving them dominion over all creation and subjecting all creation to them. It has been said: with speech, writing and understanding. There is no obstacle to understanding the honour mentioned in the verse as encompassing all of these things.

The greatest of the qualities of honour is intellect, for by it they have gained dominion over all the animals, distinguished between good and evil, expanded in foods and drinks, and acquired wealth by which they have caused the attainment of matters that animals cannot attain. By it they were able to build dwellings that protect them from what they fear, and to produce garments that shield them from heat and cold. It has been said: their honour is that He made Muhammad (ﷺ) one of them.

﴿And We carried them on land and sea﴾. This is a specification of some kinds of honour. He, glorified is He, carried them on land by means of beasts, and at sea by means of ships. It has been said: We carried them in both [land and sea], in that We did not swallow them up nor drown them.

﴿And provided for them of the good things﴾, i.e., delicious foods and drinks and all that they enjoy and benefit from. ﴿And We preferred them over many of those We created with a [marked] preference﴾. He, glorified is He, left this "many" general and did not explain its kinds. This conveys that He, glorified is He, favoured the children of Adam over many of His creatures. Some scholars have taken "many" here to mean "all," but this is a forced interpretation for which there is no need.

Many scholars have busied themselves with matters for which there is no need and from which no benefit follows, namely the question of whether the angels are superior to the prophets or the prophets to the angels. Among the proofs by which those who prefer the prophets over the angels have held is this verse, but it offers no evidence for their claim, given what you have come to know of the generality of "many" and the failure to specify it. The partisanship in this question is what drove some of the Ash'aris to interpret "many" here as "all," so that the preference over the angels might be established for them. Some of the Mu'tazilites have also taken this verse as evidence for the superiority of the angels over the prophets, but there is no evidence in it for that. For it has not been established that the angels are among the small group excluded from this "many." Even if we concede that, there is nothing in what is excluded from this "many" that indicates they are superior to the children of Adam. At most, the only thing it establishes is that man was not preferred over them. It is therefore possible that they are equal to man, and possible that they are superior to him. With such possibilities, the inference is not complete. The emphasis conveyed by the phrase ﴿with a [marked] preference﴾ indicates the greatness of this preference and that it holds a firm place. Therefore, the children of Adam should receive it with gratitude and beware of ingratitude toward it.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿yuzji﴾ (drives): he said, "yujri" (runs). They also related from Qatada, who said: "He moves them through the sea."

Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿hasiban﴾ (a violent wind of stones): he said, "A rain of stones."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Qatada, who said: "Stones from the sky."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿qasifan min al-rih﴾ (a violent wind of storm): he said, "The one that drowns."

Abu 'Ubayd and Ibn al-Mundhir related from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: "The *qasif* and the *'asif* are in the sea."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿qasifan﴾: he said, "'Asifan" (a violent wind). And regarding His saying ﴿Then you will not find for yourselves against Us any avenger for it﴾: he said, "A helper."

Al-Tabarani, al-Bayhaqi in *al-Shu'ab*, and al-Khatib in his *Tarikh* related from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is nothing more honoured by Allah on the Day of Resurrection than the son of Adam." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, not even the angels?" He said: "Not even the angels. The angels are compelled, in the position of the sun and the moon." Al-Bayhaqi related it through another route, from Ibn 'Amr as a *mawquf* (a statement of a companion) report, and said: "This is the sound one."

Al-Bayhaqi in *al-Shu'ab* related from Abu Hurayra, who said: "The believer is more honoured by Allah than His angels."

Al-Tabarani related from Ibn 'Amr, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The angels said: 'O Lord, You have given the children of Adam the world, in which they eat, drink and wear clothing, while we glorify You with Your praise and do not eat, drink or play. So, just as You have given them the world, give us the Hereafter.' He said: 'I will not make the righteous offspring of those whom I created with My own hand like those to whom I said "Be," and it was.'"

'Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Jarir related it from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: "The angels said..."

The chain of al-Tabarani is thus: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sadaqa al-Baghdadi narrated to us; Ibrahim ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Khalid al-Misisi narrated to us; Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us; Abu Ghassan Muhammad ibn Mutarrif ibn Sulaym narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, from the Prophet (ﷺ), and he mentioned it.

Ibn 'Asakir related through the route of 'Urwa ibn Ruwaym, who said: "Anas ibn Malik narrated to me from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)," and he mentioned something similar to the first hadith of Ibn 'Amr, with an addition.

Al-Bayhaqi also related something similar in *al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat* through another route, from 'Urwa ibn Ruwaym, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said..." and he mentioned it.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Shu'ab* related through various routes from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿And We have certainly honoured the children of Adam﴾: he said, "We made them eat with their hands, while all other creatures eat with their mouths."

Al-Hakim in *al-Tarikh* and al-Daylami related from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Honour is eating with the fingers."
