Then God, glorified is He, concluded this verse with His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And you have not been given of knowledge except a little.﴾ That is: the knowledge that God has taught you is nothing but a small amount in comparison with the knowledge of the Creator, glorified is He, even if you have been given a large share of knowledge. Indeed, the knowledge of the prophets, peace be upon them, in comparison with the knowledge of God, glorified is He, is nothing but what a bird takes in its beak from the sea, as in the hadith of Musa and al-Khidr, peace be upon them both.

'Abd al-Razzaq, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shayba, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim (who graded it sound), and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "*Duluk al-shams* is its setting (*ghurubuha*). The Arabs say, when the sun sets: *dalakat al-shams* (the sun has declined)."

Ibn Abi Shayba and Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ali, who said: "*Duluquha* is its setting."

'Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shayba, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas, who said, regarding ﴿at the decline of the sun﴾: "The departure of the sun (*zawal al-shams*)."

al-Bazzar, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Daylami transmitted from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: '*Dulūk al-shams* is its departure (*zawaluha*).'" al-Suyuti graded its chain as weak. Malik transmitted it in the Muwatta', and 'Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Ibn Abi Shayba, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted it from Ibn 'Umar as his own statement.

'Abd al-Razzaq transmitted from him, who said: "*Duluk al-shams* is its inclination (*ziyaguha*) after midday."

Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn Jarir transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "*Duluquha* is its departure (*zawaluha*)."

Ibn Abi Shayba and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from him, regarding God's saying ﴿at the decline of the sun﴾, that he said: "When the shade (*al-fay'*) begins to move."

Ibn Jarir transmitted from Abu Mas'ud and 'Uqba ibn 'Amr, who both said: "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: 'Gabriel came to me at the decline of the sun, when it had passed its zenith, and led me in the noon prayer (*al-zuhr*).'"

Ibn Jarir transmitted from Abu Barza al-Aslami, who said: "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, used to pray the noon prayer when the sun had passed its zenith, then he recited: ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun﴾."

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted something similar from a hadith of Anas. Among what is cited as evidence that *al-duluk* is the zenith of midday is what Ibn Jarir transmitted from Jabir, who said: "I invited the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, and whomever of his companions wished to be fed at my house. Then they left when the sun had passed its zenith. The Prophet, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, went out and said: 'Go out, O Abu Bakr, for this is the time when the sun has declined (*dalakat*).'" There is an unknown narrator in its chain. However, Ibn Jarir transmitted it from him by another route, from Sahl ibn Bakkar, from Abu 'Awana, from al-Aswad ibn Qays, from Nubayh al-'Anbari, from Jabir, and mentioned something similar, traced to the Prophet (*marfu'an*).

al-Tabarani transmitted from Ibn Mas'ud regarding God's saying ﴿until the darkness of the night﴾, that he said: "Until the late evening prayer (*al-'isha' al-akhira*)."

Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "*Ghasaq al-layl* is the gathering of the night and its darkness."

Ibn Jarir transmitted from him, who said: "*Ghasaq al-layl* is the beginning of the night."

'Abd al-Razzaq transmitted from Abu Hurayra, who said: "*Duluk al-shams* is when the sun leaves the middle of the sky, and *ghasaq al-layl* is the setting of the sun."

Ibn Jarir transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas regarding God's saying ﴿and the Qur'an of dawn﴾, that he said: "It is the dawn prayer (*salat al-subh*)."

Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi (who graded it sound), al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim (who graded it sound), Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in *Shu'ab al-Iman* transmitted from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, regarding God's saying: ﴿and the Qur'an of dawn; indeed, the Qur'an of dawn is ever witnessed﴾. He said: "The angels of the night and the angels of the day witness it, and they gather in it." It is in the two *Sahihs* from him, as a marfu' report, with the wording: "The angels of the night and the angels of the day gather at the dawn prayer." Then Abu Hurayra said: "Recite, if you wish: ﴿and the Qur'an of dawn; indeed, the Qur'an of dawn is ever witnessed﴾."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Tabarani transmitted something similar from Ibn Mas'ud as a mawquf report.

(p. 840)

Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim, Ibn Jarir, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Indeed, the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed﴾. He said: "The angels of the night and the angels of the day witness it."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿as an additional [prayer] for you﴾, that he said: "That is specific to the Prophet (ﷺ). He was commanded to pray the night vigil, and it was made obligatory upon him."

al-Tabarani in al-Awsat and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated from Aishah that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Three things are obligatory upon me, and for you they are a sunnah: the witr, the siwak, and the night prayer."

Ahmad, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Umamah, regarding His words: ﴿as an additional [prayer] for you﴾, that he said: "It was an additional [prayer] for the Prophet (ﷺ), and for you it is a virtue." In another wording: "The additional prayer was only specific to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi, who graded it hasan, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding His words: ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾, and when he was asked about it, he said: "It is the praiseworthy station, in which I will intercede for my ummah."

Ahmad (p-841), Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, al-Hakim, who graded it sahih, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ka'b ibn Malik that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "People will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection, and I and my ummah will be on a hill, and my Lord will clothe me in a green garment. Then I will be given permission, and I will say what Allah wills me to say. That is the praiseworthy station."

al-Bukhari and others narrated from Ibn Umar, who said: "On the Day of Resurrection every nation will follow its prophet, saying: 'O so-and-so, intercede! O so-and-so, intercede!' until the intercession reaches the Prophet (ﷺ). That is the day on which Allah will raise him to a praiseworthy station."

He also narrated something similar to it from him, as a marfu' report. The narrations on this subject are very numerous and firmly established in the two Sahihs and elsewhere, so we will not lengthen by mentioning them. Whoever wishes for a full survey should examine the hadiths on intercession, including the intercession of the mothers and others.

al-Tabarani narrated, regarding His words: ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾, that he said: "He will seat him between Himself and Jibril, and he will intercede for his ummah. That is the praiseworthy station."

al-Daylami narrated from Ibn Umar, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: (﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾) he said: 'He will seat me with Him upon the throne.'" It is necessary to investigate the chain of narration of these two hadiths.

Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, who graded it sahih, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, who graded it sahih, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu'aym, al-Bayhaqi and al-Diya in al-Mukhtarah narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) was in Makkah, and then he was commanded to emigrate. So Allah revealed: ﴿And say: My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance and to exit a sound exit, and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority﴾."

al-Hakim, who graded it sahih, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il narrated from Qatadah regarding His words: (﴿And say: My Lord, cause me to enter﴾), the verse, that he said: "Allah brought him out of Makkah with a sound exit, and brought him into Madinah with a sound entrance."

He said: The Prophet of Allah knew that he had no capacity for this matter except through an authority, so he asked for a supporting authority for the Book of Allah, His limits and His obligations, and for establishing the Book of Allah. For authority is a might from Allah, which He placed among His servants. Were it not for that, some of them would raid others, and the strong among them would devour the weak.

al-Khatib narrated from Umar ibn al-Khattab, who said: "By Allah, what Allah restrains by authority is greater than what He restrains by the Qur'an."

al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) entered Makkah, and around the House were three hundred and sixty idols. He began striking them with a stick in his hand, saying: ﴿Truth has come and falsehood has vanished; indeed, falsehood is ever bound to vanish﴾, and ﴿Truth has come, and falsehood can neither originate nor restore﴾ [Saba': 49]." There are hadiths on this subject as well.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Mujahid regarding His words: (﴿And turns away with his side﴾), that he said: "He withdrew."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: (﴿was ever despairing﴾), that he said: "Despairing." And regarding His words: ﴿Each acts according to his manner﴾, he said: "according to his side."

Hannad and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from al-Hasan, who said: "According to his manner, according to his intention."

al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "I was walking with the Prophet (ﷺ) among the ruins of Madinah, and he was leaning on a palm-frond stalk. He passed by a group of Jews, and some of them said to others: 'Ask him about the spirit.' Some of them said: 'Do not ask him.' They said: 'O Muhammad, what is the spirit?' He continued leaning on the stalk, so I thought he was receiving revelation. Then he said: ﴿They ask you about the spirit. Say: The spirit is of the command of my Lord, and you have been given of knowledge only a little﴾."

Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, who graded it sahih, al-Nasa'i, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Hibban, Abu al-Shaykh in al-Azamah, al-Hakim, who graded it sahih, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu'aym and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The Quraysh said to the Jews: 'Give us something to ask this man.' They said: 'Ask him about the spirit.' So it was revealed: ﴿They ask you about the spirit. Say: The spirit is of the command of my Lord, and you have been given of knowledge only a little﴾. They said: 'We have been given much knowledge; we have been given the Torah, and whoever has been given the Torah has been given much good.' So Allah revealed: ﴿Say: If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord are exhausted, even if We brought the like of it as a supplement﴾ [al-Kahf: 109]." There are hadiths and reports on this subject.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 17, verses 86–93 (part 1 of 2):

When Allah, glory be to Him, had explained that He had given them only a little knowledge, He explained that, if He willed to take away this little from them, He would do so, and He said: ﴿And if We willed, We would surely take away that which We have revealed to you.﴾ The lam is the lam of preparation (al-lam al-muwatti'ah), and "la-nadhhabanna" (surely We would take away) is the answer to the oath, standing in place of the answer to the conditional.

Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is: if We willed, We would erase it from the hearts and from the books until no trace of it would be found. End of quote.

He referred to the Qur'an with the relative pronoun (alladhi) to magnify its status. ﴿Then you would not find for yourself against Us any advocate concerning it,﴾ that is, concerning the Qur'an, ﴿(any) guardian (wakil)﴾ against Us, meaning: you would not find anyone who would take charge of Us in restoring any part of it after We had taken it away.

As for the exception in His words, ﴿except as a mercy from your Lord﴾: if it is a connected exception (istithna' muttasil), its meaning is: except that your Lord has mercy upon you, so We do not take it away. If it is a disconnected exception (istithna' munqati'), its meaning is: but your Lord does not will that, as a mercy from your Lord; or: but a mercy from your Lord has left it not taken away. ﴿Indeed, His favour upon you has been great,﴾ in that He made you a messenger, sent down the Book to you, made you the master of the children of Adam, gave you the praiseworthy station (al-maqam al-mahmud), and other blessings with which He favoured you.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, argued against the polytheists by the inimitability of the Qur'an, saying: ﴿Say: "If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur'an,﴾ revealed from Allah, described with the lofty attributes of perfect eloquence, excellence of composition and solidity of expression, ﴿they would not produce its like,﴾ where the noun is made explicit in the place where a pronoun would be expected. He did not suffice with saying "they would not produce the like of it" referring to the mentioned like, in order to repel the suspicion that there might be a specific like of it, and to indicate that the intended meaning is the negation of a like of it in any description whatsoever. This is the answer to an omitted oath, as indicated by the lam of preparation, and it stands in place of the answer to the conditional.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, made clear their inability to oppose it, whether the one who undertakes it is each of them individually or the whole collectively in support, saying: ﴿and even if they were to one another assistants.﴾ That is, helpers and supporters. The answer to "law" (even if) is omitted, and the estimated meaning is: "and even if they were to one another assistants, they would not produce its like." Thus it is established that they will not produce its like in any circumstance. The aspect of the Qur'an's inimitability has already been discussed at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah in relation to this verse, as a refutation of what the disbelievers said: ﴿If we willed, we would surely say the like of this﴾, and as a denial of them.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, explained that the disbelievers, despite their inability to oppose it, persisted in their disbelief and failure to believe, saying: ﴿And We have certainly diversified for the people in this Qur'an from every example,﴾ that is, We have repeated the discourse in it with every example that calls for reflection: signs, lessons, encouragement and warning, commands and prohibitions, the stories of the earlier peoples, Paradise and Hell, and the Resurrection. ﴿But most of the people refused except disbelief.﴾ Meaning: from the people of Makkah, for they denied and rejected that the Qur'an is the speech of Allah after the proof had been established against them, and they demanded from the signs what was not theirs to demand. He used the noun in the place where a pronoun would be expected, saying ﴿but most of the people refused﴾, for emphasis or clarification. Since "abā" (refused) is interpreted as a negation, meaning "did not accept" or "was not pleased," the exception from it, His saying ﴿except disbelief﴾, is valid.

﴿And they said: "We will not believe you﴾, that is, the chiefs of Makkah said, such as Utbah and Shaybah, the two sons of Rabi'ah, Abu Sufyan and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith. Then they made the negation of their belief dependent upon an end they requested, saying: ﴿until you cause to gush forth for us from the earth a spring.﴾ Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and 'Asim read "tafjura" (cause to gush) without the doubled letter, like "taqtula." The rest read it with the doubled letter. They did not differ concerning "fatufajjira al-anhar" (so that you cause the rivers to gush forth) that it is doubled. Abu Hatim explained this by saying that the first is followed by "yanbu'" (spring), which is singular, while the second is followed by "al-anhar" (rivers), which is plural.

It was answered that although "yanbu'" is singular in form, what is meant by it is the plural, for "yanbu'" refers to springs that do not dry up.

It is objected that "yanbu'" is the spring of water, and its plural is "yanabi'," and it is only said of a spring that it is "yanbu'" when it is abundant and its nature is to gush forth without interruption; and the letter ya' is extra, like "ya'bub" (one who drinks water in large gulps).

﴿Or you have a garden﴾, that is, an orchard whose trees cover its ground. The meaning: suppose you do not cause the rivers to gush for our sake, then cause them to gush for your own sake, by ﴿having a garden of palm trees and grapevines, and you cause rivers to gush forth within it abundantly,﴾ that is, you make them flow with force, ﴿within it in gushing abundance.﴾

﴿Or you cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces, as you have claimed,﴾ Mujahid read "aw tasquṭa" (or it falls), with the sky as its subject. All the others read "aw tuskita" (or you cause to fall), in the second person, meaning: or you, O Muhammad, cause the sky to fall.

"Kisaf" with a fatha on the sin is the plural of "kisfah," which is the reading of Nafi', Ibn 'Amir and 'Asim, and "kisfah" means a piece. The rest read "kisfan" with a sukun on the sin.

Al-Akhfash said: whoever reads with a sukun on the sin takes it as singular, and whoever reads with a fatha takes it as plural.

Al-Mahdawi said: it is permissible that, in the reading with a sukun, it is the plural of "kisfah," and it is permissible that it is a verbal noun (masdar).

Al-Jawhari said: "al-kisfah" is a piece of something; it is said: "give me a kisfah of your garment," and the plural is "kisaf" and "kusuf"; and it is said that "al-kisaf" and "al-kisfah" are the same. The accusative of "kisafan" is in the position of a circumstantial accusative (hal). The kaf in "kama za'amta" (as you claimed) is in the place of the accusative, as an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, meaning: a falling similar to what you claimed, by which they mean the words of Allah, glory be to Him: ﴿If We will, We shall cause the earth to swallow them, or cause pieces of the sky to fall upon them﴾ [Saba': 9]. Abu 'Ali said: "al-kisf" with a sukun is the cut piece, like "al-tahn" is to the ground grain, and its derivation, according to Abu Zayd, is from "kasaftu al-thawb kisafan," meaning when you cut it.

Al-Zajjaj said: from "kasaftu al-shay'," meaning when you covered it; as if it was said: "or you cause it to fall upon us as a covering."

﴿Or you bring Allah and the angels before us as a guarantee (qabilan).﴾ The commentators differed concerning the meaning of "qabilan." It was said: its meaning is "in direct observation" (mu'ayanah); this was said by Qatadah and Ibn Juraij, and Abu 'Ali al-Farisi chose it, saying: if you take it to mean direct observation, then "al-qabil" is a verbal noun, like "al-nakir" and "al-nadhir."

It was said: its meaning is "a guarantor (kafil)," said by al-Dahhak. It was said: "a witness (shahid)," said by Muqatil. It was said: it is the plural of "qabilah" (tribe), meaning you bring the kinds of angels tribe by tribe; said by Mujahid and 'Ata'. It was said: "a surety (dhamin)." It was said: "facing us (muqabilan)," like "al-'ashir" and "al-mu'ashir."

﴿Or you have a house of gold,﴾ that is, of gold; this is how Ibn Mas'ud read it. Its root meaning is adornment, and "al-muzakhraf" means the decorated, and "zakhharif al-ma'" are its currents. Al-Zajjaj said: it is adornment, returning to the original meaning of "zukhruf," but this is far-fetched, for the meaning would become: "or you have a house of adornment." ﴿Or you ascend into the sky,﴾ that is, you climb up its ladders. It is said: "raqaytu fi al-sullam" (I ascended the ladder) when you climb and mount. Similar to it is ﴿nor will we believe in your ascension,﴾ meaning because of your ascension, and it is a verbal noun, like "madha yamdi mudiyyan" and "hawa yahwi hawiyyan." ﴿Until you send down to us a book we may read.﴾ That is, until you send down to us from the sky a book that confirms you and indicates your prophethood, which we read all together, or which each one of us reads. It was said: its meaning is a book from Allah to each one of us, as in His words: ﴿Rather, each man among them desires to be given scrolls spread out﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 52].

Then Allah, glory be to Him, commanded His Messenger, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace, to say something expressing amazement at their words and glorifying the Lord, glory be to Him, above their ugly demands, so He said: ﴿Say: "Glory be to my Lord!"﴾, that is, a declaration of Allah's transcendence above being incapable of anything.

The people of Makkah and Syria read: "qala subhana rabbi" (he said: Glory be to my Lord), meaning the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace.

﴿Am I anything but a human being,﴾ one of mankind, not an angel who would ascend to the sky, ﴿a messenger?﴾ commanded by Allah, glory be to Him, to convey to you. Have you heard, O you who make these demands, that any human has been able to do any of them? And if you mean that I ask this from Allah, glory be to Him, so that He would show it through my hands, then a messenger, if he brings one single miracle, that suffices him, for through it his truthfulness becomes clear, and there is no necessity to seek more. I am a servant under command; it is not for me to impose upon my Lord what is not necessary and what no need calls for. If I were obliged to respond to every obstinate person, every opponent would propose proposals at every moment and demand for himself the showing of signs. Exalted is Allah above what the wrongdoers say, a great exaltation, far removed from their obstinacy, and sanctified above their proposals.

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim (and he authenticated it), Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab have transmitted, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Indeed this Qur'an will be lifted. It was said: How will it be lifted when Allah has fixed it in our hearts and we have set it down in the codices? He said: It will be taken away in a single night, so that no verse of it remains in a heart or a codex except that it is lifted, and you will wake up with none of it among you." Then he recited: ﴿And if We willed, We would surely take away that which We have revealed to you.﴾ This has been related from him through several chains.

Ibn 'Adi transmitted from Abu Hurairah, traced to the Prophet, something similar.

Muhammad ibn Nasr transmitted from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr something similar, as a statement of his own (mawquf).

al-Daylami in Musnad al-Firdaws transmitted from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, traced to the Prophet, something similar also.

Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, transmitted from Abu Hurairah as a statement of his own (mawquf), something similar also.

Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Daylami transmitted from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, traced to the Prophet, something similar also.

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Jabir, traced to the Prophet, something similar also.

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn 'Umar, traced to the Prophet, something similar.

Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas who said: "Mahmud ibn Shaykhan, Nu'aymLan ibn Asi, Bahri ibn 'Amr and Salam ibn Mishkam came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace, and they said: Tell us, O Muhammad, about this which you have brought: is it truly from Allah? For we do not see it harmonious as the Torah is harmonious. He said to them: By Allah, you know that it is from Allah. They said: We will bring you the like of what you bring. So Allah revealed: ﴿Say: "If mankind and the jinn gathered together..."﴾ the verse."

Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from him that 'Utbah and Shaybah, the two sons of Rabi'ah, Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, a man from Banu 'Abd al-Dar, Abu al-Bukhturi, brother of Banu Usayd, al-Aswad ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, Rabi'ah ibn al-Aswad, al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, 'Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, al-'As ibn Wa'il, and Nubayh and Munabbih, the two sons of al-Hajjaj al-Sahmiyyan, gathered after sunset by the back of the Ka'bah. Some of them said to others: Send to Muhammad and speak to him and dispute with him. He mentioned a long narration including what they asked him and tested him with, and that this was the occasion of revelation of His words: ﴿And they said: "We will not believe you"﴾ up to His words: ﴿a human messenger.﴾

Its chain according to Ibn Jarir is thus: Abu Kurayb related to us, Yunus ibn Bukayr related to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to us, a shaykh from the people of Egypt, who had arrived some forty-odd years earlier, related to me, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, and he mentioned it. In it is this unknown man.

Sa'd ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Sa'id ibn Jubayr concerning His words: ﴿And they said: "We will not believe you"﴾, that he said: it was revealed concerning the maternal brother of Umm Salamah, 'Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Mujahid concerning His words: ﴿a spring﴾, that he said: "springs."

Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from al-Suddi who said: "al-yanbu' is the river that flows from the spring."

Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: ﴿Or you have a garden﴾, that he said: "an estate."

Ibn Jarir transmitted from him concerning "kisafan," that he said: "pieces."

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him (on the authority of Mujahid) regarding ﴿qabilan﴾: "Face to face."

Ibn Jarir also narrated from him regarding ﴿min zukhruf﴾: "Of gold."

Abu 'Ubayd, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn al-Anbari and Abu Nu'aym narrated from Mujahid, who said: "I did not know well what az-zukhruf meant until I heard it in the recitation of 'Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud): ﴿or you have a house of gold﴾."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him regarding His saying ﴿a book that we may read﴾: "From the Lord of the worlds to so-and-so, son of so-and-so. Every person will wake up to find a scroll placed at his head, which he will read."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 17, verses 86–93 (part 1 of 2):

When Allah, glory be to Him, had explained that He had given them only a little knowledge, He explained that, if He willed to take away this little from them, He would do so, and He said: ﴿And if We willed, We would surely take away that which We have revealed to you.﴾ The lam is the lam of preparation (al-lam al-muwatti'ah), and "la-nadhhabanna" (surely We would take away) is the answer to the oath, standing in place of the answer to the conditional.

Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is: if We willed, We would erase it from the hearts and from the books until no trace of it would be found. End of quote.

He referred to the Qur'an with the relative pronoun (alladhi) to magnify its status. ﴿Then you would not find for yourself against Us any advocate concerning it,﴾ that is, concerning the Qur'an, ﴿(any) guardian (wakil)﴾ against Us, meaning: you would not find anyone who would take charge of Us in restoring any part of it after We had taken it away.

As for the exception in His words, ﴿except as a mercy from your Lord﴾: if it is a connected exception (istithna' muttasil), its meaning is: except that your Lord has mercy upon you, so We do not take it away. If it is a disconnected exception (istithna' munqati'), its meaning is: but your Lord does not will that, as a mercy from your Lord; or: but a mercy from your Lord has left it not taken away. ﴿Indeed, His favour upon you has been great,﴾ in that He made you a messenger, sent down the Book to you, made you the master of the children of Adam, gave you the praiseworthy station (al-maqam al-mahmud), and other blessings with which He favoured you.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, argued against the polytheists by the inimitability of the Qur'an, saying: ﴿Say: "If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur'an,﴾ revealed from Allah, described with the lofty attributes of perfect eloquence, excellence of composition and solidity of expression, ﴿they would not produce its like,﴾ where the noun is made explicit in the place where a pronoun would be expected. He did not suffice with saying "they would not produce the like of it" referring to the mentioned like, in order to repel the suspicion that there might be a specific like of it, and to indicate that the intended meaning is the negation of a like of it in any description whatsoever. This is the answer to an omitted oath, as indicated by the lam of preparation, and it stands in place of the answer to the conditional.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, made clear their inability to oppose it, whether the one who undertakes it is each of them individually or the whole collectively in support, saying: ﴿and even if they were to one another assistants.﴾ That is, helpers and supporters. The answer to "law" (even if) is omitted, and the estimated meaning is: "and even if they were to one another assistants, they would not produce its like." Thus it is established that they will not produce its like in any circumstance. The aspect of the Qur'an's inimitability has already been discussed at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah in relation to this verse, as a refutation of what the disbelievers said: ﴿If we willed, we would surely say the like of this﴾, and as a denial of them.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, explained that the disbelievers, despite their inability to oppose it, persisted in their disbelief and failure to believe, saying: ﴿And We have certainly diversified for the people in this Qur'an from every example,﴾ that is, We have repeated the discourse in it with every example that calls for reflection: signs, lessons, encouragement and warning, commands and prohibitions, the stories of the earlier peoples, Paradise and Hell, and the Resurrection. ﴿But most of the people refused except disbelief.﴾ Meaning: from the people of Makkah, for they denied and rejected that the Qur'an is the speech of Allah after the proof had been established against them, and they demanded from the signs what was not theirs to demand. He used the noun in the place where a pronoun would be expected, saying ﴿but most of the people refused﴾, for emphasis or clarification. Since "abā" (refused) is interpreted as a negation, meaning "did not accept" or "was not pleased," the exception from it, His saying ﴿except disbelief﴾, is valid.

﴿And they said: "We will not believe you﴾, that is, the chiefs of Makkah said, such as Utbah and Shaybah, the two sons of Rabi'ah, Abu Sufyan and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith. Then they made the negation of their belief dependent upon an end they requested, saying: ﴿until you cause to gush forth for us from the earth a spring.﴾ Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and 'Asim read "tafjura" (cause to gush) without the doubled letter, like "taqtula." The rest read it with the doubled letter. They did not differ concerning "fatufajjira al-anhar" (so that you cause the rivers to gush forth) that it is doubled. Abu Hatim explained this by saying that the first is followed by "yanbu'" (spring), which is singular, while the second is followed by "al-anhar" (rivers), which is plural.

It was answered that although "yanbu'" is singular in form, what is meant by it is the plural, for "yanbu'" refers to springs that do not dry up.

It is objected that "yanbu'" is the spring of water, and its plural is "yanabi'," and it is only said of a spring that it is "yanbu'" when it is abundant and its nature is to gush forth without interruption; and the letter ya' is extra, like "ya'bub" (one who drinks water in large gulps).

﴿Or you have a garden﴾, that is, an orchard whose trees cover its ground. The meaning: suppose you do not cause the rivers to gush for our sake, then cause them to gush for your own sake, by ﴿having a garden of palm trees and grapevines, and you cause rivers to gush forth within it abundantly,﴾ that is, you make them flow with force, ﴿within it in gushing abundance.﴾

Al-Akhfash said: whoever reads with a sukun on the sin takes it as singular, and whoever reads with a fatha takes it as plural.

Al-Mahdawi said: it is permissible that, in the reading with a sukun, it is the plural of "kisfah," and it is permissible that it is a verbal noun (masdar).

Al-Jawhari said: "al-kisfah" is a piece of something; it is said: "give me a kisfah of your garment," and the plural is "kisaf" and "kusuf"; and it is said that "al-kisaf" and "al-kisfah" are the same. The accusative of "kisafan" is in the position of a circumstantial accusative (hal). The kaf in "kama za'amta" (as you claimed) is in the place of the accusative, as an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, meaning: a falling similar to what you claimed, by which they mean the words of Allah, glory be to Him: ﴿If We will, We shall cause the earth to swallow them, or cause pieces of the sky to fall upon them﴾ [Saba': 9]. Al-Zajjaj said: from "kasaftu al-shay'," meaning when you covered it; as if it was said: "or you cause it to fall upon us as a covering."

﴿Or you bring Allah and the angels before us as a guarantee (qabilan).﴾ The commentators differed concerning the meaning of "qabilan." It was said: its meaning is "a guarantor (kafil)," said by al-Dahhak. It was said: "a witness (shahid)," said by Muqatil. It was said: it is the plural of "qabilah" (tribe), meaning you bring the kinds of angels tribe by tribe; said by Mujahid and 'Ata'. It was said: "a surety (dhamin)." It was said: "facing us (muqabilan)," like "al-'ashir" and "al-mu'ashir."

﴿Or you have a house of gold,﴾ that is, of gold; this is how Ibn Mas'ud read it. Its root meaning is adornment, and "al-muzakhraf" means the decorated, and "zakhharif al-ma'" are its currents. Al-Zajjaj said: it is adornment, returning to the original meaning of "zukhruf," but this is far-fetched, for the meaning would become: "or you have a house of adornment." ﴿Or you ascend into the sky,﴾ that is, you climb up its ladders. The people of Makkah and Syria read: "qala subhana rabbi" (he said: Glory be to my Lord), meaning the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace.

﴿Am I anything but a human being,﴾ one of mankind, not an angel who would ascend to the sky, ﴿a messenger?﴾ commanded by Allah, glory be to Him, to convey to you. Have you heard, O you who make these demands, that any human has been able to do any of them? Then he recited: ﴿And if We willed, We would surely take away that which We have revealed to you.﴾ This has been related from him through several chains.

Ibn 'Adi transmitted from Abu Hurairah, traced to the Prophet, something similar.

Muhammad ibn Nasr transmitted from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr something similar, as a statement of his own (mawquf).

al-Daylami in Musnad al-Firdaws transmitted from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, traced to the Prophet, something similar also.

Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, transmitted from Abu Hurairah as a statement of his own (mawquf), something similar also.

Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Daylami transmitted from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, traced to the Prophet, something similar also.

Some of them said to others: Send to Muhammad and speak to him and dispute with him. Its chain according to Ibn Jarir is thus: Abu Kurayb related to us, Yunus ibn Bukayr related to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to us, a shaykh from the people of Egypt, who had arrived some forty-odd years earlier, related to me, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, and he mentioned it. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Mujahid concerning His words: ﴿a spring﴾, that he said: "springs."

Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from al-Suddi who said: "al-yanbu' is the river that flows from the spring."

Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: ﴿Or you have a garden﴾, that he said: "an estate."

Ibn Jarir transmitted from him concerning "kisafan," that he said: "pieces."

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him (on the authority of Mujahid) regarding ﴿qabilan﴾: "Face to face."

Ibn Jarir also narrated from him regarding ﴿min zukhruf﴾: "Of gold."

Abu 'Ubayd, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn al-Anbari and Abu Nu'aym narrated from Mujahid, who said: "I did not know well what az-zukhruf meant until I heard it in the recitation of 'Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud): ﴿or you have a house of gold﴾."

He referred to the Qur'an with the relative pronoun (alladhi) to magnify its status. ﴿Then you would not find for yourself against Us any advocate concerning it,﴾ that is, concerning the Qur'an, ﴿(any) guardian (wakil)﴾ against Us, meaning: you would not find anyone who would take charge of Us in restoring any part of it after We had taken it away.

As for the exception in His words, ﴿except as a mercy from your Lord﴾: if it is a connected exception (istithna' muttasil), its meaning is: except that your Lord has mercy upon you, so We do not take it away. If it is a disconnected exception (istithna' munqati'), its meaning is: but your Lord does not will that, as a mercy from your Lord; or: but a mercy from your Lord has left it not taken away. ﴿Indeed, His favour upon you has been great,﴾ in that He made you a messenger, sent down the Book to you, made you the master of the children of Adam, gave you the praiseworthy station (al-maqam al-mahmud), and other blessings with which He favoured you.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, argued against the polytheists by the inimitability of the Qur'an, saying: ﴿Say: "If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur'an,﴾ revealed from Allah, described with the lofty attributes of perfect eloquence, excellence of composition and solidity of expression, ﴿they would not produce its like,﴾ where the noun is made explicit in the place where a pronoun would be expected. He did not suffice with saying "they would not produce the like of it" referring to the mentioned like, in order to repel the suspicion that there might be a specific like of it, and to indicate that the intended meaning is the negation of a like of it in any description whatsoever. This is the answer to an omitted oath, as indicated by the lam of preparation, and it stands in place of the answer to the conditional.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, made clear their inability to oppose it, whether the one who undertakes it is each of them individually or the whole collectively in support, saying: ﴿and even if they were to one another assistants.﴾ That is, helpers and supporters. The answer to "law" (even if) is omitted, and the estimated meaning is: "and even if they were to one another assistants, they would not produce its like." Thus it is established that they will not produce its like in any circumstance. The aspect of the Qur'an's inimitability has already been discussed at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah in relation to this verse, as a refutation of what the disbelievers said: ﴿If we willed, we would surely say the like of this﴾, and as a denial of them.

He used the noun in the place where a pronoun would be expected, saying ﴿but most of the people refused﴾, for emphasis or clarification. Since "abā" (refused) is interpreted as a negation, meaning "did not accept" or "was not pleased," the exception from it, His saying ﴿except disbelief﴾, is valid.

﴿And they said: "We will not believe you﴾, that is, the chiefs of Makkah said, such as Utbah and Shaybah, the two sons of Rabi'ah, Abu Sufyan and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith. Then they made the negation of their belief dependent upon an end they requested, saying: ﴿until you cause to gush forth for us from the earth a spring.﴾ Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and 'Asim read "tafjura" (cause to gush) without the doubled letter, like "taqtula." The rest read it with the doubled letter. They did not differ concerning "fatufajjira al-anhar" (so that you cause the rivers to gush forth) that it is doubled. Abu Hatim explained this by saying that the first is followed by "yanbu'" (spring), which is singular, while the second is followed by "al-anhar" (rivers), which is plural.

It was answered that although "yanbu'" is singular in form, what is meant by it is the plural, for "yanbu'" refers to springs that do not dry up.

It is objected that "yanbu'" is the spring of water, and its plural is "yanabi'," and it is only said of a spring that it is "yanbu'" when it is abundant and its nature is to gush forth without interruption; and the letter ya' is extra, like "ya'bub" (one who drinks water in large gulps).

﴿Or you have a garden﴾, that is, an orchard whose trees cover its ground. The meaning: suppose you do not cause the rivers to gush for our sake, then cause them to gush for your own sake, by ﴿having a garden of palm trees and grapevines, and you cause rivers to gush forth within it abundantly,﴾ that is, you make them flow with force, ﴿within it in gushing abundance.﴾

Al-Mahdawi said: it is permissible that, in the reading with a sukun, it is the plural of "kisfah," and it is permissible that it is a verbal noun (masdar).

It was said: its meaning is "a guarantor (kafil)," said by al-Dahhak. It was said: "a witness (shahid)," said by Muqatil. It was said: it is the plural of "qabilah" (tribe), meaning you bring the kinds of angels tribe by tribe; said by Mujahid and 'Ata'. It was said: "a surety (dhamin)." It was said: "facing us (muqabilan)," like "al-'ashir" and "al-mu'ashir."

﴿Or you have a house of gold,﴾ that is, of gold; this is how Ibn Mas'ud read it. Its root meaning is adornment, and "al-muzakhraf" means the decorated, and "zakhharif al-ma'" are its currents. The people of Makkah and Syria read: "qala subhana rabbi" (he said: Glory be to my Lord), meaning the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace.

﴿Am I anything but a human being,﴾ one of mankind, not an angel who would ascend to the sky, ﴿a messenger?﴾ commanded by Allah, glory be to Him, to convey to you. Have you heard, O you who make these demands, that any human has been able to do any of them? And if you mean that I ask this from Allah, glory be to Him, so that He would show it through my hands, then a messenger, if he brings one single miracle, that suffices him, for through it his truthfulness becomes clear, and there is no necessity to seek more. I am a servant under command; it is not for me to impose upon my Lord what is not necessary and what no need calls for. If I were obliged to respond to every obstinate person, every opponent would propose proposals at every moment and demand for himself the showing of signs. Exalted is Allah above what the wrongdoers say, a great exaltation, far removed from their obstinacy, and sanctified above their proposals.

As for the exception in His words, ﴿except as a mercy from your Lord﴾: if it is a connected exception (istithna' muttasil), its meaning is: except that your Lord has mercy upon you, so We do not take it away. If it is a disconnected exception (istithna' munqati'), its meaning is: but your Lord does not will that, as a mercy from your Lord; or: but a mercy from your Lord has left it not taken away. ﴿Indeed, His favour upon you has been great,﴾ in that He made you a messenger, sent down the Book to you, made you the master of the children of Adam, gave you the praiseworthy station (al-maqam al-mahmud), and other blessings with which He favoured you.

Since "abā" (refused) is interpreted as a negation, meaning "did not accept" or "was not pleased," the exception from it, His saying ﴿except disbelief﴾, is valid.

It was answered that although "yanbu'" is singular in form, what is meant by it is the plural, for "yanbu'" refers to springs that do not dry up.

It is objected that "yanbu'" is the spring of water, and its plural is "yanabi'," and it is only said of a spring that it is "yanbu'" when it is abundant and its nature is to gush forth without interruption; and the letter ya' is extra, like "ya'bub" (one who drinks water in large gulps).

It was said: it is the plural of "qabilah" (tribe), meaning you bring the kinds of angels tribe by tribe; said by Mujahid and 'Ata'. It was said: "a surety (dhamin)." It was said: "facing us (muqabilan)," like "al-'ashir" and "al-mu'ashir."

He did not suffice with saying "they would not produce the like of it" referring to the mentioned like, in order to repel the suspicion that there might be a specific like of it, and to indicate that the intended meaning is the negation of a like of it in any description whatsoever. This is the answer to an omitted oath, as indicated by the lam of preparation, and it stands in place of the answer to the conditional.

**Verses 94–100**

He, glory be to Him, relates another doubt of theirs, one the Noble Book has repeatedly addressed in various places, mentioning it and refuting it. He says: ﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when the guidance came to them except that they said, "Has God sent a human as a messenger?"﴾ The meaning of "the people" is general, though it has been said that it refers specifically to the people of Makkah. That is, nothing prevented them from believing in the Qur'an and in the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), which is the second object of *mana'a* (prevented). The meaning of ﴿when the guidance came to them﴾ is that revelation came to them from God, glory be to Him, upon His Messenger, and clarified that for them and guided them to it. The interrogative particle *al-hamza* (the interrogative *alif*) in ﴿Has God sent a human as a messenger?﴾ expresses their denial that a messenger could be a human. The meaning is that this belief, which encompassed them all, namely the denial that a messenger could be of the human species, is what prevented them from believing in the Book and the Messenger. He expressed it as "saying" to indicate that it was nothing more than a mere statement they uttered with their mouths.

The meaning of *tuma'nina* (calm, at rest) is stillness, so what is meant here is residence and habitation, as one says: "So-and-so inhabited the town" when he stays in it, even if he walks about attending to his affairs. ﴿We would have sent down to them from heaven an angel as a messenger﴾ so that he would be of their kind. In this there is an announcement from God, glory be to Him, that messengers should be of the same kind as those to whom they are sent. It is as if He, glory be to Him, considered two conditions for sending a messenger of the angelic kind: the first being that the inhabitants of the earth are angels; the second being that they walk on foot, unable to fly with their wings into the heavens. For if they were able to do so, they would have flown up and heard from its inhabitants what it is necessary to know and hear, and then there would be no benefit in sending angels to them.

The likely reasoning is that the denial is directed at the messenger characterized by humanness in the first place, so by the rule of opposition it necessarily follows that the other is likewise.

Then He concluded the speech with what amounts to a threat, saying: ﴿Say, "God suffices as a witness between me and you."﴾ That is: say to them, O Muhammad, on your behalf: God alone suffices as a witness to my conveying to you what He has commanded me of the matters of the message. He said "between me and you" and did not say "between us," to establish complete separation. It has also been said that the manifestation of a miracle in accordance with the Prophet's claim is a testimony from God to his truthfulness. Then He gave the reason for His being a sufficient witness, saying: ﴿Indeed He is ever Acquainted with and Seeing of His servants﴾ That is: knowing all their conditions, encompassing their outward and inward aspects, seeing what has occurred among them and what will occur.

Then He, glory be to Him, made clear that both acceptance and rejection are dependent on His will, saying: ﴿Whomever God guides is the one guided﴾ That is: whomever God wills to guide is the one guided to the truth, or to every goal. ﴿And whomever He leaves astray﴾ That is: whomever He wills to lead astray ﴿you will not find for them protectors﴾ who would help them ﴿apart from Him﴾ meaning God, glory be to Him, and who would guide them to the truth from which God has led them astray, or to the path of salvation. His saying ﴿is the one guided﴾ follows the wording of *man* (whoever), and His saying ﴿you will not find for them﴾ follows the meaning. The address in ﴿you will not find﴾ is either to the Prophet (ﷺ) or to anyone suitable for it.

The second: they will be dragged on the Day of Resurrection upon their faces literally, as is done in this world to one whose humiliation and torment is intensified. This is the correct view, because of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day they are dragged into the Fire upon their faces﴾ [al-Qamar: 48], and because of what is authentically reported in the Sunnah, as will come. The position of ﴿upon their faces﴾ is accusative as a circumstantial phrase (*hal*) from the pronoun of the object. ﴿Blind﴾ (*'umyan*) is accusative as a circumstantial phrase, and ﴿mute and deaf﴾ (*bukman wa summan*) are conjoined to it. The *abkam* is one who does not speak, and the *asamm* is one who does not hear. This is a condition in which they are raised, in the most hideous form and the most dreadful sight. God has combined for them blindness of sight, inability to speak, and inability to hear, along with being dragged upon their faces. Then, beyond all this, ﴿their refuge is Hell﴾ That is: the place to which they return. The clause is in the accusative position as a circumstantial phrase, or it is a resumed sentence with no position. ﴿Whenever it subsides, We increase for them the blaze﴾ That is: whenever its flame dies down. It is said: "The fire subsided (*khabat*), subsiding in subsidence (*khabwan*)" when it becomes extinguished and its flame quiets.

Ibn Qutaybah (d. 276 AH) said: the meaning of ﴿We increase for them the blaze﴾ is intensification (*tasa''ur*), which is blazing.

It has been said that the subsiding of the fire implies a lightening of the punishment for its people, so how can this be reconciled with His saying: ﴿The punishment will not be lightened for them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 162]? It is answered that what is meant by the absence of lightening is that no perceptible interval of time occurs between the subsiding and the re-intensifying. It has also been said that it subsides without any lightening of their punishment from it.

﴿That﴾ That is: the punishment ﴿is their recompense﴾ which God has made obligatory for them and which they deserved from Him. The *ba'* in His saying ﴿because they denied Our signs﴾ indicates cause, that is: because of their denial of them, for they did not affirm the revealed signs nor reflect on the signs of creation. The demonstrative ﴿that﴾ is the subject (*mubtada'*), and its predicate is ﴿their recompense﴾, while ﴿because they denied﴾ is another predicate. It is also permissible for ﴿their recompense﴾ to be a second subject whose predicate is what follows it, and the whole sentence is the predicate of the first subject.

﴿And they said, "When we are bones and crumbled particles..."﴾ The *hamza* here is interrogative for denial. The exegesis of this verse has already been given in this surah. The word *khalqan* (creation) in His saying ﴿Will we really be resurrected in a new creation?﴾ is either a verbal noun from a verb of the same root (*masdar*) or a circumstantial phrase, meaning: created.

So He, glory be to Him, brought an argument that restrains them from denial and turns them back from rejection.

He said: ﴿Do they not see that God, who created the heavens and the earth, is able to create the likes of them?﴾ That is: the One who is able to create this is more able to restore what is lesser than it. It has also been said that the meaning is that He is able to annihilate them and bring others into existence. On the first view, *khalq* (creation) means restoration (*i'adah*); on this view it has its literal meaning.

The clause ﴿And He has appointed for them a term about which there is no doubt﴾ is conjoined to ﴿Do they not see﴾, and the meaning is: they have known by the evidence of reason that whoever is able to create the heavens and the earth is able to create the likes of them, because they are not stronger in creation than they. As He said: ﴿Are you more difficult to create, or is the heaven?﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 27]. ﴿And He has appointed for them a term about which there is no doubt﴾ This is death or the Resurrection. It is possible that the *waw* is for resumption of speech. It has also been said that there is inversion in the sentence, meaning: "Do they not see that God, who created the heavens and the earth and appointed for them a term about which there is no doubt, is able to create the likes of them?" ﴿But the wrongdoers refused except denial﴾ That is: the polytheists refused except to deny. In this the apparent noun is placed in the position of the pronoun, to pass judgment on them as wrongdoers and transgressors of limits.

Then, since these disbelievers requested that rivers and springs be made to flow through their lands so that their livelihoods would expand, God, glory be to Him, made clear that they would not be content, but would remain in their stinginess and niggardliness. He said: ﴿Say, "If you possessed the treasuries of my Lord's mercy..."﴾ The word ﴿you﴾ (*antum*) is nominative as the subject of a verb omitted and explained by what follows, meaning: "If you possessed—you would possess." The separate pronoun is a substitute (*badal*) for the attached pronoun, which is the *waw*. The treasuries of His mercy, glory be to Him, are the treasuries of provisions.

Al-Zajjaj said: God informed them that if they owned the treasuries of provisions, they would withhold out of stinginess and miserliness, which is fear of spending; that is, fear that they would spend and then become poor. In omitting the verb that the word ﴿you﴾ is the subject of, and in presenting the statement in the form of a subject and predicate, there is an indication that they are the ones especially characterized by niggardliness.

The lexicographers said: *anfaqa*, *asram*, *a'dama*, and *aqtara* mean "his wealth became little." So the meaning is: you would have withheld out of fear of the scarcity of wealth. ﴿And man is ever tight-fisted﴾ That is: stingy, restricting others.

It is said: *qatara 'ala 'iyalihi* (he was stingy with his dependents), *yaqturu* and *yuqattiru*, *qatran* and *qutur*: he restricted them in their provision. It is also permissible that what is meant is that man is ever [p. 845] of little wealth. The apparent meaning is that what is intended is an emphasis in describing him with niggardliness, because man is not of little wealth in general; rather some of them have much wealth. Then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Anas.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Their refuge is Hell﴾, that he said: it means that they are its fuel.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim related through 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah from him, regarding His saying ﴿Whenever it subsides﴾, that he said: it became quiet.

These same authorities also related from him regarding the verse: he said: Whenever it burns them, it kindles them as fuel. When it has burned them so that nothing of them remains, it becomes glowing embers that blaze, and that is its subsiding. Then when they are changed into a new creation, it returns to them.

'Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Qatadah regarding ﴿fear of spending﴾ that he said: fear of destitution. ﴿And man is ever tight-fisted﴾ he said: stingy and withholding.

Then He, glory be to Him, made clear that both acceptance and rejection are dependent on His will, saying: ﴿Whomever God guides is the one guided﴾ That is: whomever God wills to guide is the one guided to the truth, or to every goal. ﴿And whomever He leaves astray﴾ That is: whomever He wills to lead astray ﴿you will not find for them protectors﴾ who would help them ﴿apart from Him﴾ meaning God, glory be to Him, and who would guide them to the truth from which God has led them astray, or to the path of salvation. His saying ﴿is the one guided﴾ follows the wording of *man* (whoever), and His saying ﴿you will not find for them﴾ follows the meaning. The address in ﴿you will not find﴾ is either to the Prophet (ﷺ) or to anyone suitable for it.

The second: they will be dragged on the Day of Resurrection upon their faces literally, as is done in this world to one whose humiliation and torment is intensified. This is the correct view, because of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day they are dragged into the Fire upon their faces﴾ [al-Qamar: 48], and because of what is authentically reported in the Sunnah, as will come. The *abkam* is one who does not speak, and the *asamm* is one who does not hear. This is a condition in which they are raised, in the most hideous form and the most dreadful sight. God has combined for them blindness of sight, inability to speak, and inability to hear, along with being dragged upon their faces. Then, beyond all this, ﴿their refuge is Hell﴾ That is: the place to which they return. The clause is in the accusative position as a circumstantial phrase, or it is a resumed sentence with no position. ﴿Whenever it subsides, We increase for them the blaze﴾ That is: whenever its flame dies down. It is said: "The fire subsided (*khabat*), subsiding in subsidence (*khabwan*)" when it becomes extinguished and its flame quiets.

Ibn Qutaybah (d. 276 AH) said: the meaning of ﴿We increase for them the blaze﴾ is intensification (*tasa''ur*), which is blazing.

It has been said that the subsiding of the fire implies a lightening of the punishment for its people, so how can this be reconciled with His saying: ﴿The punishment will not be lightened for them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 162]? It is answered that what is meant by the absence of lightening is that no perceptible interval of time occurs between the subsiding and the re-intensifying. It has also been said that it subsides without any lightening of their punishment from it.

The *ba'* in His saying ﴿because they denied Our signs﴾ indicates cause, that is: because of their denial of them, for they did not affirm the revealed signs nor reflect on the signs of creation. The demonstrative ﴿that﴾ is the subject (*mubtada'*), and its predicate is ﴿their recompense﴾, while ﴿because they denied﴾ is another predicate. It is also permissible for ﴿their recompense﴾ to be a second subject whose predicate is what follows it, and the whole sentence is the predicate of the first subject.

The word *khalqan* (creation) in His saying ﴿Will we really be resurrected in a new creation?﴾ is either a verbal noun from a verb of the same root (*masdar*) or a circumstantial phrase, meaning: created.

So He, glory be to Him, brought an argument that restrains them from denial and turns them back from rejection.

He said: ﴿Do they not see that God, who created the heavens and the earth, is able to create the likes of them?﴾ That is: the One who is able to create this is more able to restore what is lesser than it. It has also been said that the meaning is that He is able to annihilate them and bring others into existence. On the first view, *khalq* (creation) means restoration (*i'adah*); on this view it has its literal meaning.

The clause ﴿And He has appointed for them a term about which there is no doubt﴾ is conjoined to ﴿Do they not see﴾, and the meaning is: they have known by the evidence of reason that whoever is able to create the heavens and the earth is able to create the likes of them, because they are not stronger in creation than they. It is possible that the *waw* is for resumption of speech. It has also been said that there is inversion in the sentence, meaning: "Do they not see that God, who created the heavens and the earth and appointed for them a term about which there is no doubt, is able to create the likes of them?" ﴿But the wrongdoers refused except denial﴾ That is: the polytheists refused except to deny. In this the apparent noun is placed in the position of the pronoun, to pass judgment on them as wrongdoers and transgressors of limits.

Then, since these disbelievers requested that rivers and springs be made to flow through their lands so that their livelihoods would expand, God, glory be to Him, made clear that they would not be content, but would remain in their stinginess and niggardliness.
